# Inspect Swarm

> Run a swarm of agents on one sample of an Inspect task.



# Inspect Swarm

## Welcome

Inspect Swarm runs a swarm of agents on one sample of an [Inspect](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk) task. A swarm is an Inspect agent, so it replaces the task’s solver, and the task’s scorer scores the swarm’s answer.

> **WARNING: Warning**
>
> Everything in Inspect Swarm is experimental and may change in any release without notice, including [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm), [member()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member), [Budget](./reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget), the built-in controller and channel names, and the record and evidence formats. No support is guaranteed.

## Getting Started

Install it from PyPI:

``` bash
pip install inspect_swarm
```

or, in a uv project:

``` bash
uv add inspect_swarm
```

To install the latest development version from GitHub:

``` bash
pip install git+https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm
```

or, in a uv project:

``` bash
uv add "inspect_swarm @ git+https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm"
```

For now it needs inspect_ai’s `main` branch, which has features no inspect_ai release has yet. Installing Inspect Swarm installs a released inspect_ai, so install inspect_ai from GitHub `main` too (in a uv project, `uv add "inspect-ai @ git+https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai"`):

``` bash
pip install git+https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai
```

It needs Python 3.11 or later.

## Run a swarm on an existing task

Pass [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) as the solver. From Python:

``` python
from inspect_ai import eval
from inspect_ai.agent import react

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm

from my_tasks import my_task

eval(
    my_task(),
    solver=swarm(members=member(react, count=4)),
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
)
```

From the command line:

``` bash
inspect eval my_tasks.py --solver inspect_swarm/swarm -S 'members={factory: react, count: 4}'
```

Each sample runs four [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) members, `react-1` to `react-4`, at the same time. Each starts with the sample’s input and a short preamble: its name, the number of members, and how to share files. The swarm stops at the first submission and uses it as its answer. The other members finish the calls they have in flight and stop. The task’s scorer scores the answer as it would score a single agent.

`--solver` and `eval(solver=...)` replace the task’s whole solver, including any system message or tools it set up, so give the members their tools and prompt. Members use the eval’s model unless they are given one. The task’s `setup` solver still runs first.

## A task with a swarm

A task can build the swarm itself. This one, from [`examples/getting_started.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/getting_started.py), makes the number of members a task parameter:

``` python
from inspect_ai import Task, task
from inspect_ai.agent import react
from inspect_ai.scorer import match
from questions import QUESTIONS

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm


@task
def getting_started(k: int = 3) -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=QUESTIONS,
        solver=swarm(members=member(react, count=k), channels=[]),
        scorer=match(),
        token_limit=200_000,
    )
```

``` bash
inspect eval examples/getting_started.py --model openai/gpt-5-mini -T k=4
```

- `channels=[]` gives the members no channel. The default, `filesystem`, tells members to share files in the sample’s sandbox, and these questions have none. See [Channels](./channels.html.md).
- The swarm takes its budget from the sample’s limits: here it stops its members at 95% of the token limit. See [Budgets](./budget.html.md).
- `-T k=1` is a swarm of one, the single-agent arm to compare with. See [Scoring](./scoring.html.md#comparisons).

## What the log shows

Each member’s events are in a timeline named after it, so the log viewer can show one member’s trajectory. The sample’s messages are its input followed by the answer’s message. When the swarm ends, it writes its result record to the transcript: each member’s state and status, and which member’s output is the answer. Read it with [swarm_result()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_result); see [Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-result-record). It also writes two entries to the sample store:

- `inspect_swarm:ledger`: the swarm’s caps and the usage and cost of each member. See [Analysis](./analysis.html.md#the-ledger).
- `inspect_swarm:metrics`: tokens, cost and time for the swarm and each member, and counts of how members acted and communicated. See [Analysis](./analysis.html.md#metrics).

## Learning more

- [Members](./members.html.md): member records, names, limits, member builders, and how a member ends.
- [Controllers](./controllers.html.md): when the swarm stops, and writing a controller of your own.
- [Channels](./channels.html.md) and [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md): how members share information, and waiting for each other.
- [Budgets](./budget.html.md) and [Sandboxes](./sandboxes.html.md): the swarm’s caps and splits, and shared or per-member sandboxes.
- [Scoring](./scoring.html.md), [Analysis](./analysis.html.md) and [Restrictions](./restrictions.html.md): the answer and the result record, metrics, the ledger, and what the swarm does not support or record.

The [examples](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/tree/main/examples) are runnable tasks for each of these. The designs behind the swarm are in [design/](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/tree/main/design).

## For agents

The documentation is also published as Markdown for agents:

- <https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_swarm/llms.txt>: an index of the pages, with a line on what each covers.
- <https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_swarm/llms-guide.txt>: the user guide as one Markdown file.
- <https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_swarm/llms-full.txt>: the user guide and the API reference as one Markdown file.


# Members – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

A member is an agent registered with `@agent`, such as [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) or [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent). Give it in one of two forms:

- The factory form: the factory and its arguments, `member(react, args={...})`. The swarm calls the factory once for each member in each sample, so every member gets its own agent. `count` makes several members from one record.
- The built form: an agent you have built, `member(react(...))`, or the agent alone. It is one member. The same agent object cannot be in two members.

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import deepagent, react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash, python
from inspect_ai.util import token_limit

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=[
        member(
            react,
            args={"tools": [bash(), python()]},
            name="solver",
            role="solve the task",
            count=3,
        ),
        member(
            deepagent(tools=[bash()]),
            name="reviewer",
            role="check the solvers' work in /shared",
            limits=[token_limit(200_000)],
        ),
    ],
)
```

This swarm has four members: `solver-1` to `solver-3` and `reviewer`. The role is added to the member’s preamble and given to the controller.

## Names

A member is named after its agent (`react`, `deepagent`) unless you give `name`. With `count` above 1 the members are `name-1` to `name-k`. Names must be unique in the swarm. They cannot be `init`, `solvers` or `scorers`, and cannot contain `/` or `#`. The [shared-memory channel](./shared-memory.html.md) also needs names that start with a lowercase letter, followed by at most 47 lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

Members left on their default name are numbered across the whole roster, not per record. So one member with a different prompt and model takes two records:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=[
        member(react, args={"prompt": "Solve the task."}, count=6),
        member(
            react,
            args={
                "prompt": "Check the others' work in /shared.",
                "model": "openai/gpt-5",
            },
        ),
    ],
)
```

The first record makes `react-1` to `react-6` and the second `react-7`.

When every copy differs, give each its own record. A list comprehension builds them:

``` python
prompts = ["Try algebra.", "Try brute force.", "Try a proof by cases."]
solver = swarm(members=[member(react, args={"prompt": p}) for p in prompts])
```

These are `react-1` to `react-3`. Names you give with `name` are not numbered across records, so give each record its own.

### Members that choose their names

With `choose_name=True` a member is not told its name. The swarm’s preamble says how many agents are in the swarm and asks it to choose a name for itself and tell the other members what it is:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=member(react, args={"tools": [bash()]}, count=4, choose_name=True),
)
```

Each member starts with `You are one of 4 agents in a swarm working on this task at the same time. Choose a name for yourself and tell the other members what it is.` Its role, if it has one, is still stated. The log still names the members `react-1` to `react-4`: the swarm’s timelines, spans, tool state, budget shares and result record use those names. The name a member chose is in its transcript, not in the swarm’s records.

A roster can mix the two, for example a lead you name and workers that name themselves. The `filesystem` channel then tells every member that its scratch directory may be taken by another member ([Channels](./channels.html.md#the-filesystem-channel)).

A swarm in which any member chooses its name can use only the `filesystem` channel or no channel (`channels=[]`). Other channels, including [shared memory](./shared-memory.html.md) and your own, show members to each other by name, so [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) refuses them.

The swarm does not change text you give the member yourself: the sample input, a controller’s `start(input=...)` and `start(preamble=...)`, the agent’s prompt, and the sandbox configuration. A controller’s `start(preamble=...)` uses its text as given, and `preamble=False` leaves the preamble out ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md)). Neither adds a request to choose a name.

## Limits

`limits` takes token, cost, turn, message and time limits for that member alone. Working limits are refused. A member that reaches one ends with status `member_limit:<type>`, and the others continue. The swarm’s own caps are set with `budget=` ([Budgets](./budget.html.md)).

A member time limit does not run while the member is held at a turn boundary by a controller’s callbacks ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#boundary-callbacks)): it counts only the time the member was not held. A member whose time limit ran out before it reached the boundary ends `member_limit:time` there, without being held.

## Member builders

A member builder is a function registered with `@agent` that builds the member’s agent. Pass it to [member()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) without calling it, with its arguments in `args`:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import Agent, agent, react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash

from inspect_swarm import member, shared_memory, swarm, swarm_tools


@agent
def worker() -> Agent:
    return react(tools=[bash(), swarm_tools()])


solver = swarm(members=member(worker, name="w", count=3), channels=[shared_memory()])
```

Use a builder for anything the swarm gives a member at run time, such as [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools) ([Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md)). The log records a builder by its name and arguments, so the swarm can be rebuilt from the log. It cannot rebuild [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools) passed in `args` or inside an agent you built.

A builder is also the place for anything each member must have its own of. Every member built from one record gets the same objects from `args`, and two built agents given the same tool object share it, across members and samples. Inspect’s built-in tools keep their state in the sample store or the sandbox, so this matters only for a custom tool or helper that keeps state in its Python object (a counter, a cache, a client). The swarm calls a builder once for each member in each sample, so what the builder creates belongs to one member. [`examples/stop_on_proof.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/stop_on_proof.py) keeps a per-member flag this way.

## Tool state

Each member runs in its own tool-state scope, named after the member. Built-in tools that keep state in the sample store ([memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory), [bash_session()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash_session), the skill tool) give each member its own state when their `instance` is left at the default, so the default [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) is private to each member.

An explicit `instance` is used as given: members that name the same instance share its state. A board shared on purpose was `memory(instance="board")` before the shared-memory channel; see [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#migrating-from-memoryinstance) for moving to the channel.

- The sample store itself is shared. State that custom tools or agent code keep in the store with no instance is shared unless they resolve their instance with [tool_state_instance()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#tool_state_instance).
- Tool state that a setup solver prepared at the default instance before the swarm runs is not visible to the members. They start with fresh state.

## Background work

Native members support `deepagent(background=True)` and integer background limits. Work started with [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background) belongs to its member and uses its limits, share and sandbox. A member limit or swarm cap ends the background task that reached it. A swarm cap also starts the swarm’s soft stop; other work gets the effective grace period to finish calls already in flight.

When the member’s agent ends, its background work gets the swarm’s grace period to finish work in flight. The swarm then cancels the rest and waits for its cleanup before the member ends. `Budget.grace=0` skips the grace wait. A controller therefore sees a member’s end only after this drain.

Start background work from the running agent, not its factory. A factory that starts it makes the member `errored`. Work started outside [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background) (an `asyncio` task, a process left running in the sandbox) is not stopped.

## How a member ends

A member’s status says how it ended:

| Status | Meaning |
|----|----|
| `submitted` | Its agent returned normally. Its output is its answer. A [persistent member](#persistent-members) is never `submitted` by a normal return: it ends `submitted` when it is stopped or ended while idle, or at the turn boundary after an answer, with its last answer as its output. |
| `unsubmitted` | Its agent returned with a `content_filter` or `model_length` stop reason, as [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) does after repeated refusals or a context overflow. A persistent member also ends `unsubmitted` when its agent returns without an answer, for example when its `on_continue` returns `False` (a cut-off). |
| `stopped` | The swarm stopped it, for example when another member submitted or the swarm’s time cap was reached, or a controller ended it ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#boundary-callbacks)). A member that reaches a turn boundary of its agent loop after the stop began ends there. |
| `share` | It used up its share of a split budget. |
| `member_limit:<type>` | It reached one of its own `limits`. |
| `member_limit:custom` | Its agent stopped itself by raising `LimitExceededError("custom", ...)` with no `source`, for example from `react(on_continue=...)`. The other members continue. |
| `swarm_cap` | Its call reached one of the swarm’s caps. |
| `cancelled` | It was cancelled, after the grace period of a stop or from outside the swarm. |
| `errored` | It raised any other error. The error ends the sample. |

For a member that is not persistent, a normal return counts as a submission for any agent other than [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react)’s two cases above. An agent that gives up in some other way and returns is treated as having answered. To make a normal return mean something stronger, such as a passed check, have the member’s builder raise a custom limit when it is not so ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#stopping-on-the-first-proof)).

## Persistent members

A persistent member stays available after it answers, so a controller can give the same member several tasks with its context intact:

``` python
member(worker(), name="worker", persistent=True)
```

When a persistent member submits, or a `react(submit=False)` member gives a reply with no tool calls, the swarm records that as one of its *answers* and holds the member *idle* at its next turn boundary. The agent loop does not return. The controller hears [MemberIdle](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberidle) and gives the member its next task with `SwarmControl.wake()`, which appends the task to the member’s conversation ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#persistent-members)). The member keeps its conversation, tool state and limits across these *activations*.

- Its limits span its whole life. Its member time limit does not run while it is idle.
- Every answer is a candidate for the swarm’s answer: `first` and `last` choose across all of them, and `choose_answer()` takes the member’s latest. An answer stays a candidate however the member ends later.
- A submission in a turn that also calls a [handoff()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#handoff) is not an answer. Nor is a refusal (`content_filter`) or a reply cut off by the context window.
- A member stopped or ended while idle ends `submitted`. A member whose loop returns without an answer ends `unsubmitted`, its earlier answers still candidates.
- While it is idle, another member’s write that is news to it reaches the controller as [MemberNews](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#membernews), and the controller decides whether to wake it ([News for idle members](./controllers.html.md#news-for-idle-members)).

Only a member whose agent is a [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react), `react(submit=False)` or [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent) loop can persist, given directly or returned by a [member builder](#member-builders). The swarm refuses every other agent before it runs: a bridged member, a custom loop, [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent) with background dispatch, and an agent that calls a loop and then checks its result (`checked_solver()` in the examples). In a swarm with [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory), a persistent member must have [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools) in its own tools, not only in a subagent’s.

## A swarm of one

`swarm(members=react(), channels=[])` is a single agent run under the swarm’s rules, with the same records. Use it as the single-agent arm when you compare a swarm with one agent ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#comparisons)). Unlike a plain agent, it returns an empty output when its member does not submit.

## Agents the swarm refuses

- ACP agents wait for their caller to drive them, so they are refused.
- Bridged members, which run a CLI agent in the sandbox through Inspect’s agent bridge, cannot have background work. See [Restrictions](./restrictions.html.md).


# Controllers – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

`controller=` decides which members start, when and with what input, and when the swarm is done. It also decides which submission is the swarm’s answer: by a rule, `first` (the default) or `last`, or by choosing a member itself ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-answer)).

## leaderless

The only built-in controller is `leaderless`, the default. It starts every member with the sample’s input and stops the swarm when the first member submits, since that submission is the answer. The other members finish the calls they have in flight and stop. Those still running after the grace period are cancelled. If no member submits, the swarm ends when all have ended.

Pass `leaderless(stop_on_submission=False)` to let every member run to its end:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react

from inspect_swarm import leaderless, member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=member(react, count=4),
    controller=leaderless(stop_on_submission=False),
)
```

Use it when:

- The scorer reads what members leave in the sandbox, where members still working change what is scored ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#scoring-what-members-leave)).
- You measure each member’s result, as for team@k.
- Your agent returns normally when it gives up, which would count as a submission and stop the swarm.

The answer is still the first submission. When the members work as a team and the latest submission should be the answer, add `final="last"`:

``` python
from inspect_swarm import leaderless

controller = leaderless(stop_on_submission=False, final="last")
```

`final="last"` needs `stop_on_submission=False`, and `leaderless` refuses it otherwise.

`leaderless` returns the stop reason `submitted` when a submission stopped the swarm and `all_done` when every member ended. The ledger records it as `stop_reason` ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#the-ledger)).

## Writing a controller

A controller is a factory decorated with `@swarm_controller` that returns a [Controller](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#controller). Its `run` function is called once per sample with a [SwarmControl](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarmcontrol), through which it starts members and receives their events. It returns a stop reason, and returning requests the stop.

``` python
from collections.abc import Sequence
from contextlib import aclosing

from inspect_swarm import (
    Controller,
    MemberEnded,
    MemberInfo,
    StopReason,
    SwarmControl,
    swarm_controller,
)


@swarm_controller
def escalate(first: str = "fast") -> Controller:
    """Start one member; start the others only if it ends without a submission."""

    def check(roster: Sequence[MemberInfo]) -> None:
        if first not in [m.name for m in roster]:
            raise ValueError(f"escalate(): no member is named {first!r}.")

    async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
        swarm.start(first)
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if isinstance(event, MemberEnded) and event.submitted:
                    return "submitted"
        for m in swarm.members:
            if m.state == "pending":
                swarm.start(m)
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if isinstance(event, MemberEnded) and event.submitted:
                    return "submitted"
        return "all_done"

    return Controller(run, check=check)
```

- `swarm.members` are the members in roster order, as [MemberHandle](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberhandle)s: name, role, state (`pending`, `running` or `ended`, and for [persistent members](#persistent-members) `idle` or `ending`), status and whether it submitted. A controller never sees what a member wrote unless it holds the member at a turn boundary ([Boundary callbacks](#boundary-callbacks)).
- `swarm.start(member, input=None, *, preamble=None)` starts a member and returns at once. `input` replaces the swarm’s input for that member; `None` gives it the swarm’s input. The member’s preamble follows either, as a user message. A member runs once, and starting one after the stop has begun raises.
- The swarm’s preamble tells each member that the members work at the same time. A controller that runs them otherwise can pass its own text as `preamble`, which replaces the whole preamble, channel instructions included, and is used as given. `preamble=False` leaves it out; the input must then hold a user message.
- `swarm.events()` yields each event once, in order from the swarm’s start. [MemberEnded](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberended) gives the member’s name, status and whether it submitted; [MemberIdle](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberidle) and [MemberNews](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#membernews) come only from [persistent members](#persistent-members). Test an event’s type before reading its fields. The iterator ends when no member is running or ending and no event is waiting, so a member started or woken later needs a new `events()` call. Use one iterator at a time, and close it, as `aclosing()` does here.
- `check`, if given, is called with the roster when [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) is called. Raise `ValueError` for a roster the controller cannot run.
- `final`, if given, is the rule that chooses the answer: `first` (the default, as here) or `last`.
- The stop reasons `all_done`, `submitted`, `verified` and `quiescence` are recorded as they are. Any other is recorded as `controller:<reason>`.

A [Controller](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#controller) holds configuration only: one object serves every sample, so keep per-sample state in `run`’s local variables. The factory’s arguments are logged with the controller, so it can be rebuilt from the log. Pass the controller to the swarm, `swarm(..., controller=escalate("fast"))`, or by its registered name with its default arguments, `controller="escalate"`.

### Choosing the answer

A controller can choose the answer itself. `swarm.choose_answer(member, reason=None)` names a member that has ended with a submission, and its submission is then the answer, whatever the `final` rule says. For a persistent member, it takes the member’s latest answer at the time of the call, and keeps that one if the member answers again. A controller chooses once. The record gives the mode `controller` and the reason ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-result-record)).

This controller answers with the first submission from a member with a given role, and falls back to the `final` rule, `first`, when none of them submits:

``` python
from contextlib import aclosing

from inspect_swarm import (
    Controller,
    MemberEnded,
    StopReason,
    SwarmControl,
    swarm_controller,
)


@swarm_controller
def prefer(role: str) -> Controller:
    """Answer with the first submission from a member with this role, if any."""

    async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
        for m in swarm.members:
            swarm.start(m)
        chosen = False
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if (
                    not chosen
                    and isinstance(event, MemberEnded)
                    and event.submitted
                    and swarm.member(event.member).role == role
                ):
                    swarm.choose_answer(event.member, reason=f"first {role} to submit")
                    chosen = True
        return "all_done"

    return Controller(run)
```

## Boundary callbacks

A controller can hold a member between the turns of its agent loop. `handle.on_boundary(callback, origin=...)` registers a callback that runs at every turn boundary of the member’s own loop: before its first generation and before each one after it, with no model or tool call of the loop in flight. It returns a function that unregisters the callback from the next boundary.

The callback gets a [Boundary](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#boundary):

- `member` and `index`: the member, and the boundary’s number, 0 before the first generation.
- `after`: what the conversation ends with: `start` at index 0, `tools` after a tool result, `reply` after an assistant reply with no tool calls, `wake` after a persistent member’s wake input, `user` after anything else.
- `activation`: 0 until a persistent member is first woken, then one more at each wake.
- `messages` and `output`: copies of the member’s conversation and of its last output. Changing them changes nothing.

It returns `None` to let the member go on, a list of messages to go on with that conversation, or `"end"` to end the member `stopped`. A returned list keeps each message’s id, and must hold a user message. The member gets copies of the returned messages, so changing them later changes nothing.

While its callbacks run the member is held: `handle.held` is `True`, its time limit does not run, and `swarm_wait` does not count it as active. A callback can wait as long as it likes. Its own model calls count towards the member’s limits. Its time counts as working time unless it marks its idle waits with [suspend_working_limit()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#suspend_working_limit):

``` python
import anyio
from inspect_ai.util import suspend_working_limit

from inspect_swarm import Boundary, StopReason, SwarmControl


async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
    go = anyio.Event()

    async def wait_for_go(boundary: Boundary) -> None:
        if boundary.index == 0:
            with suspend_working_limit():
                await go.wait()
        return None

    swarm.member("worker").on_boundary(wait_for_go, origin="scheduler")
    swarm.start("worker")
    ...
```

Several callbacks run in the order they were registered, each receiving the conversation as the ones before it left it. So callers compose: a pause registered after a scheduler holds the member after the scheduler lets it go.

`handle.end(origin=...)` ends a member from outside the chain, `stopped`, with the reason `ended by <origin>`. A held member ends at once: the waiting callback is cancelled and no change from that boundary is applied. A member in the middle of a turn ends at its next boundary, and its next model call is refused. If the member is still running after the swarm’s grace period, its cleanup included, it is cancelled and ends `cancelled`. The same deadline applies when a callback returns `"end"`. A member whose agent returns after `end()` ends `stopped`, whatever its output.

A swarm stop ends every member at its next boundary, and a held member at once.

Only members whose agent runs an Inspect agent loop, such as [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) or [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent), reach a boundary. Subagents and other nested loops run inside a turn of the member’s loop and are not held on their own. `on_boundary()` raises `ValueError` for a bridged member and for [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent) with background dispatch. A member with background work running when it reaches a boundary with callbacks, a member that starts a second agent loop after its first ended, and a member whose callbacks never ran because it never reached a boundary all end `errored`.

The swarm records each boundary where callbacks ran, and each change they made, by message id and hash ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#boundary-callbacks)).

## Persistent members

A [persistent member](./members.html.md#persistent-members) answers, then waits *idle* at its next turn boundary for its next task. The controller hears [MemberIdle](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberidle), with the member’s name and the index of the answer it just gave, and wakes the member with `swarm.wake(member, input)`. The input is a string or a list of user messages, appended to the member’s conversation. Each wake message gets a new id, so one list can be passed to several wakes.

This controller gives one worker each task in turn, and makes its last answer the swarm’s:

``` python
from contextlib import aclosing

from inspect_swarm import (
    Controller,
    MemberIdle,
    StopReason,
    SwarmControl,
    member,
    swarm,
    swarm_controller,
)


@swarm_controller
def dispatch(tasks: list[str], worker: str = "worker") -> Controller:
    """Give `worker` each task in turn, waking it after each answer."""

    async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
        pending = list(tasks)
        swarm.start(worker, input=pending.pop(0))
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if isinstance(event, MemberIdle) and pending:
                    swarm.wake(event.member, input=pending.pop(0))
        return "quiescence" if swarm.member(worker).state == "idle" else "all_done"

    return Controller(run, final="last")


swarm(
    members=[member(worker_agent, name="worker", persistent=True)],
    controller=dispatch(tasks),
)
```

- `wake()` takes only an `idle` member. An event can be stale by the time the controller reads it (an earlier event’s handling may have woken or ended the member), so check `swarm.member(name).state == "idle"` first.
- An idle member is held: `handle.held` is `True`, its time limit does not run, and `swarm_wait` does not count it as active. Boundary callbacks run after the wake, with `after == "wake"` and the input as the last messages.
- `handle.end()` or the swarm’s stop on an idle member sets it `ending` at once, and it ends `submitted`, with its last answer as its output. The iterator waits for its [MemberEnded](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberended).
- The swarm is *quiescent* when every member is pending, idle or ended and no event is waiting: `events()` ends. Nothing moves until the controller starts, wakes or ends a member. A controller that wakes no one returns `quiescence`.
- `leaderless` treats [MemberIdle](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberidle) as a submission, so by default the first answer stops the swarm. With `stop_on_submission=False` it returns `quiescence` once no member is working and some are idle. It never wakes a member.

### News for idle members

An idle member is not in a tool call, so it cannot see what other members write. The controller is told instead. When a record is delivered that would end a `swarm_wait` of the idle member’s own loop watching everything, such as another member’s write to the shared memory or a message sent to it with `wake=True`, the controller gets [MemberNews](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#membernews): the idle member, the channel, the record’s id and the name of the member that sent it. The controller decides whether to wake the member.

- `MemberIdle.news` says whether the member already had news when it went idle: a write it did not look at during its activation. No [MemberNews](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#membernews) reports that write, so a controller that wakes members on news also wakes on `MemberIdle.news`.
- A file stays news to the member until its own loop views it. A member that leaves a file unviewed is reported with `news` set every time it goes idle, so its prompt should tell it to view what the status line names before it answers.
- Two records give two events. Check that the member is still idle before waking it.
- A member gets no news unless its own loop has [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools).

[`examples/lead_and_workers.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/lead_and_workers.py) is a lead that hands out tasks on the shared memory to persistent workers. Its controller wakes a worker on the lead’s writes and stops when the lead ends:

``` python
@swarm_controller
def lead_and_workers(lead: str = "lead") -> Controller:
    async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
        for m in swarm.members:
            swarm.start(m)
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if isinstance(event, MemberEnded) and event.member == lead:
                    if event.submitted:
                        swarm.choose_answer(lead, reason="the lead's answer")
                        return "submitted"
                    return "lead_ended"
                woken = (isinstance(event, MemberNews) and event.sender == lead) or (
                    isinstance(event, MemberIdle) and event.news
                )
                if woken and swarm.member(event.member).state == "idle":
                    swarm.wake(event.member, WAKE)
        return "all_done"

    return Controller(run)
```

Every worker is woken on each of the lead’s writes, so a worker with no new task answers at once. The workers’ answers are reports on their own tasks, so the controller makes the lead’s submission the answer with `choose_answer()`.

## Stopping on the first proof

Some tasks have a checker, such as a proof checker or a test suite, and the experiment wants to stop when the first member’s answer passes it. [`examples/stop_on_proof.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/stop_on_proof.py) has such a controller:

``` python
from contextlib import aclosing

from inspect_swarm import (
    Controller,
    MemberEnded,
    StopReason,
    SwarmControl,
    swarm_controller,
)


@swarm_controller
def until_proved() -> Controller:
    """Start every member, and stop the swarm when the first one ends `submitted`.

    Valid only when a member's normal return means a passed check, as `checked_solver()` makes it.
    """

    async def run(swarm: SwarmControl) -> StopReason:
        for m in swarm.members:
            swarm.start(m)
        async with aclosing(swarm.events()) as events:
            async for event in events:
                if isinstance(event, MemberEnded) and event.submitted:
                    return "proved"
        return "all_done"

    return Controller(run)
```

It records the stop reason `controller:proved`. But it is right only under a precondition: a member’s normal return must mean that its answer passed the check. A [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) member also returns normally when it runs out of attempts, after three refusals, or after a context overflow it could not recover from. Without the precondition, `until_proved` can stop every member on a member that gave up, and record `controller:proved` with nothing proved.

The member’s builder makes the precondition hold. It raises a member-local custom limit when its agent returns without a passing check, which ends that member as `member_limit:custom` while the others continue:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import Agent, AgentAttempts, AgentState, agent, react
from inspect_ai.scorer import Value, value_to_float
from inspect_ai.util import LimitExceededError


@agent
def checked_solver(attempts: int = 5) -> Agent:
    """A `react()` member that returns normally only when one of its submissions passed the task's scorer."""
    passed = False
    to_float = value_to_float()

    def score_value(value: Value) -> float:
        nonlocal passed
        result = to_float(value)
        passed = passed or result == 1.0
        return result

    inner = react(attempts=AgentAttempts(attempts, score_value=score_value))

    async def execute(state: AgentState) -> AgentState:
        state = await inner(state)
        if not passed:
            # with no `source`, this ends only this member, as member_limit:custom
            raise LimitExceededError(
                "custom",
                value=0,
                limit=0,
                message="returned without a passing check",
            )
        return state

    return execute
```

- The check here is the task’s own scorer, which `react(attempts=...)` runs on each submission but the last. A last submission is never checked, so it is not a proof, and `attempts` must be at least 2 for any submission to be checked.
- The builder is called once for each member in each sample, so `passed` belongs to one member.
- With this builder, the default `leaderless` would stop at the first proof too, recording `submitted` rather than `controller:proved`.
- With background work, a controller sees a member’s end only after the member’s background work has drained ([Members](./members.html.md#background-work)), so the other members stop up to one grace period later.

[`examples/proof_swarm.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/proof_swarm.py) uses the same controller with per-member sandboxes and a checking service in its own container. Its member builder checks the answer the member leaves when the agent returns, not only the checks the agent asked for, since a member could pass a check and then change its answer.


# Channels – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

`channels=` decides how members share information. There are three built-in channels:

- `filesystem`, the default: a convention for sharing files in a sandbox, stated in each member’s preamble. It adds no tools.
- `shared_memory`: a board of files that members read and write with a tool, with a record of every write and read. See [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md).
- `messages`: direct messages between members, with a record of every message and read. See [Messages](./messages.html.md).

`channels=[]` gives members no channel instructions. Channels change what members are told and what tools they get, not what they can reach: members share the sample’s sandbox whatever the channels, unless they have their own ([Sandboxes](./sandboxes.html.md)).

A channel is given as an object, `filesystem(...)`, or by its registered name with its default arguments, `"filesystem"`. Each channel can be given once.

## The filesystem channel

`filesystem` tells each member, in its preamble, to share files in `/shared`, to read and append to `/shared/notes.md`, and to keep its own work in `/scratch/<member>`. It does not create these directories. Change the paths with `filesystem(...)`:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react

from inspect_swarm import filesystem, member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=member(react, count=4),
    channels=[filesystem(shared="/work/shared", scratch="/work/{member}")],
)
```

A member that chooses its own name ([Members](./members.html.md#members-that-choose-their-names)) is told to keep its work in `/scratch/<your name>`, a directory named with the name it chose, and to check that no other member uses the same one. The members you named are still told `/scratch/<member>`, and, when any member chooses, that a member that chooses could pick the same directory, so they check that no other member uses it.

When members have their own sandboxes and each sandbox mounts one shared volume, use `filesystem(shared_volume=True)`. Set `shared=` to the absolute path where the volume is mounted; `notes=` must be inside it. The preamble then says that `shared` and the notes file in it are the same in every member’s sandbox, and gives no scratch directory, since each sandbox is already private. The swarm cannot check that the volume is mounted, and it refuses `shared_volume=True` when members share the sample’s sandbox. See [Sandboxes](./sandboxes.html.md#a-shared-volume).

[`examples/shared_sandbox.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/shared_sandbox.py) runs [bash()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash) members in one container with this channel.

## Shared files are observed, not recorded

The filesystem channel opens no state and offers no tools, so no tool of the swarm’s carries file traffic. What the log has is each member’s own tool calls ([bash()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash), [python()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#python), [text_editor()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#text_editor)), as [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s.

Those tool calls are evidence that members may have communicated through files, not a complete record. Processes a member starts in the sandbox can read and write files between logged tool calls, and after the member has ended. A bridged member’s file operations are the CLI’s own tools, which leave no [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent) at all. An experiment that attributes communication to the filesystem must state this limit, or add its own instrumentation, such as filesystem snapshots or audit logs in the sandbox.

The same holds for every other path between members that the swarm does not carry:

- A built-in tool given the same explicit `instance` in several members, such as `memory(instance="board")`, shares its state through the sample store. Members’ [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s record its use, and nothing else does. See [Members](./members.html.md#tool-state).
- A tool that reads the transcript sees the other members’ model and tool calls ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-record-belongs-to-the-swarm)).

Channels limit what members are told, not what they can do. An arm meant to have one channel only, or none, needs members that cannot reach each other otherwise: their own sandboxes, and no shared tool instances.

## Writing a channel

A channel is a factory decorated with `@swarm_channel` that returns a [Channel](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel). A channel that only adds instructions, as `filesystem` does, subclasses [Channel](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel) and overrides `instructions()`:

``` python
from inspect_swarm import Channel, MemberInfo, swarm_channel


class LeadChannel(Channel):
    def __init__(self, lead: str) -> None:
        self.lead = lead

    def instructions(self, member: MemberInfo) -> str | None:
        if member.name == self.lead:
            return "Write the plan to /shared/plan.md before you start."
        return f"Read /shared/plan.md, which {self.lead} writes, before you start."


@swarm_channel
def lead(name: str) -> Channel:
    """Tell members that one of them writes a plan for the others."""
    return LeadChannel(name)
```

`instructions()` returns text for the member’s preamble, or `None` to add nothing. `check()`, if overridden, is called with the roster when [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) is called and raises `ValueError` for a roster the channel cannot serve. A [Channel](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel) holds configuration only: one object serves every sample. The factory’s arguments are logged with the channel.

A channel with tools and records, as `shared_memory` is, also sets `name` and `prefix` and returns a [ChannelState](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channelstate) from `open()` for each run of the swarm; its records go through the swarm’s bus. Its `reach` decides which of a member’s loops get its tools from [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools): `"loop"` (the default), only the member’s own loop; `"member"`, also the nested loops the member’s agent gives [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools). The agent decides which nested loops get [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools); `reach` filters the channel tools they get and which channels can wake their `swarm_wait`. A channel whose reads consume something for the member, such as an inbox that marks messages read, keeps `"loop"`, so that a subagent cannot read what the member’s own loop then never sees. `shared_memory` sets `"member"`: a view consumes nothing, and each loop keeps its own seen state. A channel’s tools are given to the member as they are: with the `messages` channel, their results do not count the member’s unread messages, as the swarm’s own tools do. A member learns of messages from those, or by calling `list_members`. [swarm_bridged_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_bridged_tools) serves only the built-in [messages()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#messages) and [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory) channels, so [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) refuses a bridged member beside a custom channel with records ([Restrictions](./restrictions.html.md#channels-for-bridged-members)).

This channel keeps a notice board. Any member posts a notice, and every member reads them all:

``` python
from collections.abc import Mapping

from inspect_ai.tool import Tool, ToolDef, ToolError
from pydantic import JsonValue

from inspect_swarm import (
    Bus,
    Channel,
    ChannelRun,
    ChannelState,
    Draft,
    MemberInfo,
    Record,
    calling_member,
    swarm_channel,
)


class NoticesState:
    def __init__(self, bus: Bus) -> None:
        self.bus = bus
        self.notices: list[Record] = []

    def tools(self) -> list[Tool]:
        async def post_notice(text: str) -> str:
            """Post a notice that every member can read.

            Args:
                text: The notice.
            """
            delivery = await self.bus.deliver(Draft("notices", "notice", payload=text))
            return f"Posted {delivery.record.id}."

        async def read_notices() -> str:
            """Read the other members' notices."""
            caller = calling_member()
            assert caller is not None
            shown = [r for r in self.notices if r.sender != caller.member]
            self.bus.read("notices", [r.id for r in shown])
            lines = [f"{r.id} from {r.sender}: {r.payload}" for r in shown]
            return "\n".join(lines) or "No notices."

        return [ToolDef(post_notice).as_tool(), ToolDef(read_notices).as_tool()]

    def validate(self, record: Record) -> None:
        if not record.payload.strip():
            raise ToolError("A notice needs text.")

    def admit(self, record: Record) -> None:
        pass

    def apply(self, record: Record) -> tuple[list[str], Mapping[str, JsonValue] | None]:
        self.notices.append(record)
        return [], None


class Notices(Channel):
    name = "notices"
    prefix = "n"

    def open(self, run: ChannelRun) -> ChannelState:
        return NoticesState(run.bus)

    def instructions(self, member: MemberInfo) -> str | None:
        return "Post what others should know with post_notice, and read theirs with read_notices."


@swarm_channel
def notices() -> Channel:
    return Notices()
```

Members get the tools from [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools), as with the built-in channels. A tool hands the bus a [Draft](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#draft), and `run.bus.deliver()` makes the [Record](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#record), binds the sender from the calling member, checks it, and calls the state’s `validate()`, then `admit()` and `apply()` with no `await` between them, so what `admit()` checks still holds when `apply()` runs. After address resolution and validation, the log records accepted sends and refusals by liveness, payload and storm checks or `admit()` as `sent` events. Each delivered record also has a `delivered` event. Earlier refusals, including a stopping swarm, produce no communication event. A refusal raises [ToolError](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#toolerror), which the member sees as the tool’s result.

A draft with no `to` is unaddressed: it reaches nobody directly, and the channel decides whom it concerns. `apply()` returns the members the record is news to and a JSON mapping, both written in the `delivered` event, and may name members that have not started or have ended. A draft addressed with `to=` is refused if a member it names has not started, is ending or has ended.

[calling_member()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#calling_member) tells a tool which member it acts for: a [Caller](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#caller) with the member’s name, whether the calling loop is a nested one, and that loop’s agent span. It comes from the runtime, never from model output, and is `None` outside a member of a swarm.

A tool whose result shows the channel’s records reports them with `run.bus.read(name, records)`, using the [ChannelRun](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channelrun) that `open()` was given: `name` is the channel’s `name`, and `records` are the ids of the records the result shows. A waiting channel’s `news()` reports them in `WaitNews(lines, files, depends_on=[...])`. The log records them as the result’s `depends_on`, the records the member’s later work depends on, which [the critical path](./analysis.html.md#the-critical-path) links. Two rules decide what a result depends on:

- A result that tells the loop a record was committed, without showing its content, as a wait does, depends on it.
- A result built from several records, such as a file made by several writes, depends on them all. Pass them as `depends_on=` when they differ from the records the result shows.

A channel that reports nothing adds no dependency. Every id must be a record the channel committed in this run, or the call raises `ValueError`.

`read()` returns the read’s id (`r-5`), which the log’s `read` event carries. Pass `listing=True` for a result that shows what exists rather than its content, which the metrics count as a listing, not a read.

See the docstrings of [Channel](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel), [ChannelRun](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channelrun), [ChannelState](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channelstate), [Bus](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#bus), [Draft](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#draft), [Delivery](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#delivery), `calling_member`, [WaitingState](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#waitingstate) and [WaitNews](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#waitnews) in the [reference](./reference/index.html.md).


# Shared Memory – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

[shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory) gives the swarm one board of files that every member reads and writes with a `shared_memory` tool. The tool has the commands of Inspect’s [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) tool, over files under `/shared_memory`, and one more, `append`. Every write goes through the swarm as a record from the member that made it, so the log keeps the board’s whole history, and members hear about each other’s changes.

Members that get `shared_memory` also get `swarm_wait`, so a member that needs a peer’s work waits instead of polling. Each sample has its own board, which is gone when the swarm ends.

[`examples/shared_memory.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/shared_memory.py) is a runnable swarm that splits a count between members, who share their parts on the board and wait for each other.

## Wiring

Members get the tool from [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools), which gives a member the tools of the swarm’s channels. Call it inside a member builder registered with `@agent`, and pass the builder to [member()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) without calling it:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import Agent, agent, deepagent, react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash

from inspect_swarm import (
    filesystem,
    member,
    shared_memory,
    swarm,
    swarm_tools,
)


@agent
def solver_member() -> Agent:
    return react(tools=[bash(), swarm_tools()])


@agent
def reviewer_member() -> Agent:
    return deepagent(tools=[bash(), swarm_tools()])


solver = swarm(
    members=[
        member(solver_member, name="solver", count=3),
        member(reviewer_member, name="reviewer"),
    ],
    channels=[filesystem(), shared_memory()],
)
```

- The log records a builder by name and arguments, so the swarm can be rebuilt from the log. It cannot rebuild [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools) passed in `args` or inside an agent you built ([Members](./members.html.md#member-builders)).
- Any agent that takes a [ToolSource](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#toolsource) in its tools can take [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools). It gives no tools when the swarm has no channel with tools, or outside a swarm, so one member definition serves every arm of an experiment.
- This swarm keeps the `filesystem` channel beside the board. `channels=[shared_memory()]`, or `channels=["shared_memory"]`, replaces it: members still share the sample’s sandbox, but their preamble no longer mentions `/shared`. Members with their own sandboxes can use the board with no shared volume.
- The channel needs member names that start with a lowercase letter, followed by at most 47 lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
- A bridged member gets the tool from `swarm_bridged_tools(["shared_memory"])`. Its CLI is one agent to the board: a file any of its conversations viewed counts as viewed by all of them ([Bridged members](./restrictions.html.md#bridged-members)).

## The tool

The `shared_memory` tool’s commands are `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `append`, `delete`, `rename` and `changes`. Paths are `/shared_memory` followed by up to eight components of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

- Each file has an id, such as `f-3`, which it keeps through renames. Status lines and `swarm_wait` results name files by id. `view` takes an id as `file_id`, in place of `path`. A view shows the file’s path, which the write commands take.
- A file view shows the file inside a `<peer_file>` fence that names its id, path, version and last writer. A directory view lists every file under it at any depth, with its id, version and last writer.
- Write commands return a short acknowledgment, not the file. View a file to see it.
- Every result ends with a status line naming the files other agents changed since this loop last viewed them, such as `Shared memory: 2 files changed since you last viewed them (f-2, f-9).` It names at most 10 files and counts the rest, as in `(f-1, ..., f-10, and 2 more)`. With the [messages](./messages.html.md) channel, a result in the member’s own loop then ends with its count of unread messages, when any remain.
- `changes` returns the board’s status line, naming every changed file, or `Shared memory: no files changed since you last viewed them.`, so a loop can check for news without viewing anything. Like the status line, it marks nothing seen. With `messages`, its result in a member’s own loop also ends with the unread count, when any remain.

### Fences are labels

A fence is a label for the reader, not a security boundary. A member can write text that looks like a fence, another member’s file, or text the swarm writes, such as a status line. The swarm does not refuse or clean such text.

What holds:

- Members see each other’s text only in tool results.
- The record of the board comes from the swarm’s own events and ids, never from the text of a result ([The record of the board](#the-record-of-the-board)).

An experiment that needs stronger guarantees, such as a study of members that deceive each other, needs a channel that provides them ([Writing a channel](./channels.html.md#writing-a-channel)).

### The seen rule

A loop must view a file in its current version before it overwrites it with `create`, inserts into it, renames it or deletes it. A write to a file changed since the loop’s last view is refused with an error that names the file and its last writer, and the loop views it and retries. So no member overwrites a change it has not seen.

Two commands need no view:

- `str_replace` fails unless `old_str` occurs exactly once in the file as it is when the write lands, so it is safe without one.
- `append` adds text on a new line at the end of the file as it is when the write lands, and creates the file if needed. It suits a log or list that many members write to.

## Hearing about changes

The swarm adds no messages to a member’s conversation. A member learns what other agents changed only through its tools:

- The status line at the end of every `shared_memory` result. With the [messages](./messages.html.md) channel, a result in the member’s own loop then ends with its count of unread messages.
- `shared_memory(command="changes")`, which returns the board’s status line, naming every changed file, to check for changes without viewing anything.
- `swarm_wait`, which blocks until a file the member watches changes ([Waiting for other members](#waiting-for-other-members)).

A changed file stays in the status line until the loop views it. A deleted file is listed only to a loop that previously viewed or wrote it, including a blind append. These lists hold counts, file ids and member names, never a file path or file contents.

## Waiting for other members

`swarm_wait` blocks until there is something for the member to look at:

- A file it watches has a change that the waiting agent did not write and has not viewed. It watches one file with `file_id`, a file or directory with `path`, or the whole board with neither. A subagent’s write counts, so a member can wait for its own subagents.
- Another member has ended.

It returns at once if that is already so, and keeps returning while such a file stays unviewed. Its result names the changed files by id and the ended members by name and status, never file content: the member views a file to read it.

A wait also ends without news: when every member is waiting, has ended or has not started; when the swarm stops; when the member’s own agent finishes; or after `timeout` seconds. `max_wait` sets the longest wait and the default `timeout`, 600 seconds unless you change it, for example `shared_memory(max_wait=300)`.

A wait is time inside a tool call. It counts towards the member’s time limit, the swarm’s time cap and the sample’s time and working limits. It makes no model call, so it adds no tokens, cost or steps. The metrics report each member’s waits, their time, and its `idle_time`: the seconds the member did nothing but wait ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#waits)).

A swarm with only the `filesystem` channel, or `channels=[]`, has no `swarm_wait`: there is nothing it could wake on.

## Subagents

A member’s subagents read and write the board as the member. deepagent’s [general()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#general) subagents, synchronous and background, and any nested loop given [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools), get the `shared_memory` and `swarm_wait` tools.

The member’s agent decides which subagents get [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools). deepagent’s [general()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#general) inherits the member’s tools, so it gets the board. [research()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#research) gets its own read-only tools instead, and has the board only when you pass `research(extra_tools=[swarm_tools()])`.

- Their writes are records from the member. The evidence also names the loop that made each write or read, and marks a subagent’s as `nested`.
- Each loop has its own view of the board: the seen rule and the status line apply to the loop that calls the tool.
- A member’s subagents share its write rate, so they cannot multiply its write volume.
- A subagent’s wait counts in the member’s `wait_time` but not its `idle_time`.

A deepagent member also has a private [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) of its own by default. Pass `deepagent(memory=False)` when the board should be its only memory tool.

## Limits

The board is bounded:

| Argument | Default | Limit |
|----|----|----|
| `max_files` | 10,000 | Files on the board |
| `max_file_bytes` | 1,000,000 | UTF-8 bytes in one file |
| `max_file_lines` | 100,000 | Lines in one file |
| `max_board_bytes` | 100,000,000 | UTF-8 bytes in all files together |
| `rate` | `(60, 60.0)` | Writes per member, all its loops together, in a sliding window of seconds; `None` for no limit |
| `max_wait` | 600 | The longest `swarm_wait`, in seconds, and its default timeout |

A write that would pass a limit is refused with an error that says which. Once the swarm begins to stop, writes are refused and views still work.

## The record of the board

The swarm logs the members’ writes, views and waits as [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent)s with source `inspect_swarm`. Each is in the span of the tool call that made it, and its `kind` is one of:

- `sent`: a write that reached the swarm, with its payload in `send.record.content`, why it was refused in `send.rejected` if it was, and its operation in `data["record"]["op"]`.
- `delivered`: a write applied to the board, with its commit sequence number in `delivery.seq` and each file’s previous and new version in `data["result"]["files"]`. Replaying the delivered writes in sequence order rebuilds every version of the board.
- `read`: a view or a listing. `record_ids` names the record that last wrote each file at the version shown, and `data` has each file’s version. `data["depends_on"]` names the records the result depends on: for a view, every write in the file’s history; for a deleted file’s id, the delete; for a listing, none.
- `waited`: a `swarm_wait` call, with what ended it and how long it took in `wait`, and in `data["depends_on"]` the write it reported for each changed file.

Each event names the member that acted (`agent`) and its loop (`loop_span_id`). The `record_ids` of a write’s `sent` and `delivered` events and of the reads of what it wrote are the same id. `depends_on` names each record once per loop: a record that an earlier result of the same loop depended on is left out. The [metrics](./analysis.html.md#communication) count these events for each member.

## Monitoring with Inspect Sentinel

A native member’s call to `shared_memory` is an ordinary tool call, so [Inspect Sentinel](https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_sentinel)’s tool stages see it with no swarm code. A protocol at `BeforeToolCall` can reject a write before it reaches the board, and one at `AfterToolCall` sees exactly what a view is about to show. For example, a rule that keeps credentials off the board:

``` python
from inspect_sentinel import (
    BeforeToolCall,
    Context,
    Decision,
    Escalations,
    Protocol,
    call_text,
    find_words,
    protocol,
)


@protocol
def no_secrets_on_board() -> Protocol:
    """Reject shared_memory writes that mention a credential."""

    async def decide(
        context: Context, step: BeforeToolCall, escalations: Escalations
    ) -> Decision | None:
        if step.call.function != "shared_memory":
            return None
        if step.call.arguments.get("command") == "view":
            return None
        used = find_words(call_text(step.call), ["password", "api_key", "token"])
        if used:
            return Decision.reject(
                f"write mentions {', '.join(used)}",
                message="Credentials may not be written to shared memory.",
            )
        return Decision.proceed()

    return decide
```

Pass it to the task as `Task(..., sentinel=no_secrets_on_board())`. The member gets the decision’s message as the tool call’s error. A step’s `conversation` is the agent span id of the loop that made the call, and each [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent) names that loop in `loop_span_id`, so the two can be joined. Sentinel does not run on bridged tool calls; use the bridge’s approval policies for those calls.

## Migrating from `memory(instance=...)`

Before this channel, a board shared on purpose was a [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) tool with an explicit instance in every member’s tools, `memory(instance="board")`, with the prompt saying it is shared. That still works, and it is a different channel: members’ [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s record its use, with no sender, fence, status line, bounds or [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent)s. Nothing refuses using both; an arm that wants the board as its only channel gives no two members a shared instance.

To move a task to the channel:

1.  In the member builder, replace `memory(instance="board")` with [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools) in the tools. The builder stays a registered `@agent`.
2.  For a deepagent member, pass `memory=False` to keep one memory tool as before, or leave deepagent’s private [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) as an extra notebook per member. These are different experimental conditions.
3.  Replace the instructions that described the board with `"shared_memory"` or `shared_memory(...)` in `channels=`. Its instructions go in each member’s preamble.
4.  Change the prompt’s tool and path names (`memory`, `/memories`) to `shared_memory` and `/shared_memory`.

What changes for the members:

- Overwriting with `create`, `insert`, `delete` and `rename` need a current view ([The seen rule](#the-seen-rule)), and `append` adds an entry at the end of a file without one.
- Writes return an acknowledgment, not a snippet of the file.
- A directory view lists every file under it at any depth, and there are no empty directories.
- Paths are narrower, files and the board are bounded, and tabs are kept.
- Views are fenced and name the last writer, and status lines report changes.

An eval set comparing the two boards runs them as two arms: the channel list and the builder’s arguments differ, so their task identifiers do. [`examples/proof_swarm.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/proof_swarm.py) is shaped like such a port: members with their own sandboxes whose only channel is the board.


# Messages – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

[messages()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#messages) lets members address each other. A member sends with `send_message` and reads what was sent to it with `read_messages`. `list_members` shows who is in the swarm and whether each member is still running. Every message goes through the swarm as a record from the member that sent it, so the log keeps who sent what to whom and when it was read.

The swarm adds no messages to a member’s conversation. A member hears about new messages only through its tools.

## Wiring

Members get the tools from [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools), as for [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#wiring). Call it inside a member builder registered with `@agent`:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import Agent, agent, react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash

from inspect_swarm import filesystem, member, messages, swarm, swarm_tools


@agent
def worker() -> Agent:
    return react(tools=[bash(), swarm_tools()])


solver = swarm(
    members=member(worker, count=4),
    channels=[filesystem(), messages()],
)
```

- Only the member’s own loop gets the tools. Its subagents, such as a deepagent member’s [general()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#general), do not, so each inbox has one reader.
- The channel can be combined with [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory). Then the member’s own loop gets both channels’ tools and one `swarm_wait` for both.
- The channel needs member names that start with a lowercase letter, followed by at most 47 lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`. `all` and `swarm` are reserved.
- A bridged member gets the tools from `swarm_bridged_tools(["messages"])`. All of its CLI’s conversations, subagents included, share its inbox: a message any of them reads is read ([Bridged members](./restrictions.html.md#bridged-members)).

## The tools

`send_message(to, message, reply_to=None, wake=True)` sends a message and returns its id, such as `Sent m-3 to worker-2.`

- `to` is a member name, a list of names, or `"all"` for every other running member.
- `reply_to` is the id of a message the sender sent or read, which this one answers.
- `wake=False` sends a message that does not end the recipient’s `swarm_wait`.

A send is refused, and reaches no one, when an address is not a running member other than the sender, or when one of the [limits](#limits) is passed. A message to a member that has ended, or has not started, is refused rather than kept.

`read_messages()` returns the member’s unread messages, oldest first, and marks them read:

    2 messages, oldest first.

    <peer_message id="m-9" from="worker-2" to="worker-1, worker-3">
    ...
    </peer_message>
    <peer_message id="m-14" from="worker-4" to="worker-1" reply_to="m-6">
    ...
    </peer_message>
    1 more unread message; call read_messages() again.

One read returns as many whole messages as fit in a bound set by `max_bytes` and the roster, and always at least one. The generate config’s `max_tool_output` does not apply to it, so a message is never cut. `read_messages` never waits; `swarm_wait` does.

`list_members()` lists the members in roster order, with each one’s role, its state (`pending`, `running` or `ended`) and, once it has ended, its status, such as `submitted`. It marks the caller with `(you)`, and ends with the caller’s count of unread messages.

### Fences are labels

As in [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#fences-are-labels), a fence is a label for the reader, not a security boundary. A message is delivered as it was typed, so a member can write text that looks like another member’s message or a status line. The record of messages comes from the swarm’s own events and ids, never from the text of a result.

## Hearing about messages

While a member has unread messages, the results of the swarm’s own tools in its own loop end with a line that counts them, such as `You have 2 unread messages.`: `send_message`, `list_members`, `shared_memory` and `swarm_wait`. `list_members` also says when there are none, so a member can call it to check for messages. A `read_messages` result says how many remain unread instead. The tools of other channels, yours or Inspect’s, carry no count. These lines hold counts only, never message text. Errors have no count: a member that gets one sees the count on its next result. A tool output limit smaller than the line can cut it, since the limit applies after the line is added. A member’s subagents cannot read its messages, so their results do not count them.

`swarm_wait` returns while the member has unread messages sent with `wake=True`, and names their senders: `2 unread messages (from worker-2, worker-4). Call read_messages() to read them.` It keeps returning until the member reads them. A result with other news too, such as a changed file or an ended member, also ends with the count. Messages sent with `wake=False` do not end a wait, but a wait that returns for another reason counts them. It also returns when another member ends, when every member is waiting, has ended or has not started, when the swarm stops, or after `timeout` seconds, as described in [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#waiting-for-other-members). `max_wait` sets the longest wait, 120 seconds unless you change it. With [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory) too, the longer of the two channels’ `max_wait` applies.

A member busy in a long tool call hears nothing until the call ends.

## Limits

| Argument | Default | Limit |
|----|----|----|
| `max_bytes` | 8,000 | UTF-8 bytes in one message |
| `max_unread` | 50 | Unread messages one member may have; a send that would pass it is refused |
| `rate` | `(20, 60.0)` | Messages per member in a sliding window of seconds; a message to several members counts once; `None` for no limit |
| `dedupe` | `True` | Refuse a message whose text a recipient still has unread from the same sender |
| `max_wait` | 120 | The longest `swarm_wait`, in seconds, and its default timeout |

An empty message is refused. Once the swarm begins to stop, sends are refused and reads still work.

## The record of messages

The swarm logs messages as [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent)s with source `inspect_swarm`, each in the span of the tool call that made it. Its `kind` is one of:

- `sent`: a send that reached the swarm, with its addresses, recipients, text and `reply_to` in `send.record`, why it was refused in `send.rejected` if it was, and `wake` in `data["record"]`. An inbox that is full, or a duplicate, is refused by the control `admit`.
- `delivered`: a message delivered, with its recipients and commit sequence number in `delivery`.
- `read`: a `read_messages` result, with the ids of the messages it showed in `record_ids` and the messages it depends on in `data["depends_on"]`. A read that showed nothing has no event.
- `waited`: a `swarm_wait` call, with what ended it and the unread messages it named. A wait that reports unread messages depends on all of them (`data["depends_on"]`), including those sent with `wake=False`. A wait that ends with only the unread count depends on none.

`depends_on` names each message once per loop, so a read of messages that an earlier wait reported depends on none of them.

The [metrics](./analysis.html.md#communication) count these events for each member.

A native member’s calls to `send_message` and `read_messages` are ordinary tool calls, so [Inspect Sentinel](https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_sentinel)’s tool stages see them, as in [Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#monitoring-with-inspect-sentinel).


# Budgets – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

A swarm takes its budget from the sample’s limits. With the default `Budget()`, it reads the sample’s cost, token and time limits when it starts and stops its members at 95% of each. The other 5% (`reserve`) covers calls already in flight when the swarm stops.

After a stop, members have up to `grace` seconds (default 120) to finish calls already in flight. If the sample has a time limit, this period is capped at half its remaining time. Members still running are then cancelled.

Set the caps yourself with [Budget](./reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget):

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react

from inspect_swarm import Budget, member, swarm, swarm_resources

solver = swarm(
    members=member(react, args={"tools": [swarm_resources()]}, count=4),
    budget=Budget(cost=20.0, time=1800, split="equal"),
)
```

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|----|----|----|
| `cost` | `None` | Cost cap in dollars. `None` derives it from the sample’s cost limit, or sets no cap under `derive=False`. |
| `tokens` | `None` | Token cap. A string such as `"output:1m"` keeps its metering type. `None` derives it from the sample’s token limit, or sets no cap under `derive=False`. |
