| `time` | `None` | Seconds after which the swarm stops its members. `None` derives it from the sample’s time limit, or sets no cap under `derive=False`. |
| `reserve` | `0.05` | Fraction of each sample limit held back when a cap is derived. |
| `split` | `"pool"` | How the cost and token caps are divided between members ([Splits](#splits)). |
| `grace` | `120.0` | Seconds members have, at most, to finish calls in flight after a stop. |
| `derive` | `True` | Whether a cap left `None` is derived from the sample’s limit ([No derived caps](#no-derived-caps)). |

Every field is a plain value, so each can be a task parameter. A member whose call reached a cap ends `swarm_cap`, and the swarm then stops the others ([Members](./members.html.md#how-a-member-ends)). The ledger records the caps, each member’s usage and what stopped the swarm ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#the-ledger)).

## No derived caps

With `Budget(derive=False)`, the swarm derives no caps. The sample’s own cost, token and time limits then end the swarm as they end any solver: the limit’s error propagates out of the swarm, and later solvers do not run. A cap you set explicitly still applies, and `reserve` has no effect.

As in any solver, a limit error that a tool or handoff turns into a tool message does not end the run. The member’s next model call raises the error again, as does any other member’s. A swarm cap, by contrast, stops the swarm even when a tool turns its error into a message.

A split needs a cost or token cap, so with no explicit cap use `split="pool"`.

## Cost data

A cost cap needs cost data for every member’s model, and so does a sample cost limit under `derive=False`. The swarm checks this when it starts and raises an error naming the models that have none. Configure prices with [set_model_cost()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#set_model_cost) or `--model-cost-config`.

## Splits

`Budget.split` divides the cost and token caps between members:

- `"pool"` (default): members share one budget, and any member may spend all of it.
- `"equal"`: each member gets an equal share.
- A tuple of weights, one per member in roster order: `(1, 1, 2)` gives the third member half.

A member that uses up its share stops with status `share`. Its unused share is not given to the others, so the split stays a fixed condition of the experiment. The swarm’s caps still apply above the shares: when a call reaches a cap and a share at once, the cap wins, and the swarm stops with `swarm_cap`.

## What members see

When the swarm has a cap, each member’s preamble says how the budget is split. The [swarm_resources()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_resources) tool, as in the example above, lets a member check the swarm’s caps, how much all members have used, and its own share. Code inside a member can read the same with [swarm_budget()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_budget).

A tool that reads [sample_limits()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sample_limits) shows the sample’s limits, not the swarm’s caps, so with derived caps it overstates what members can spend. Under `derive=False`, the sample’s limits can still end the run, and [swarm_resources()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_resources) shows only the caps given explicitly.

## Sweeps

Agent count, budget and split are task parameters, so they can be swept. [`examples/budget_sweep.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/budget_sweep.py):

``` python
from typing import Literal

from inspect_ai import Task, task
from inspect_ai.agent import react
from inspect_ai.scorer import match
from questions import QUESTIONS

from inspect_swarm import Budget, member, swarm, swarm_resources


@task
def budget_sweep(
    k: int = 4, budget: float = 1.0, split: Literal["pool", "equal"] = "pool"
) -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=QUESTIONS,
        solver=swarm(
            members=member(react, args={"tools": [swarm_resources()]}, count=k),
            channels=[],
            budget=Budget(split=split),
        ),
        scorer=match(),
        cost_limit=budget,
    )
```

The task sets the sample’s cost limit once, and the swarm derives its cap from it, so a single-agent arm reads the same number. Three sweeps:

- Matched budget: vary `k` at a fixed `budget` with `split="pool"`. `k=1` is the single-agent arm.
- Agent count × per-agent budget `b`: vary `k` and `b`, with `budget = k * b` and `split="equal"`. Each member’s share is `b * 0.95`.
- Split as an ablation: hold `k` and `budget` fixed and vary `split`.

For example, `inspect eval examples/budget_sweep.py -T k=8 -T budget=8 -T split=equal`. Compare arms on the cost the log records, not on the cap ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#samples-dataframe)).


# Sandboxes – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

A swarm has one of two sandbox topologies:

- Shared, the default: every member works in the sample’s sandbox, at the same time. Members can share files, and can change files under each other.
- Per member: each member works in a sandbox environment of its own, and members cannot reach each other’s. What they share goes through a channel, such as the [shared-memory board](./shared-memory.html.md), or a volume every member’s sandbox mounts.

## Shared

With no `sandbox=` on any member, members share the sample’s sandbox. The default `filesystem` channel gives them a convention for it: `/shared` for shared files, `/shared/notes.md` for notes, and `/scratch/<member>` for each member’s own work ([Channels](./channels.html.md#the-filesystem-channel)). The channel does not create these directories, so create them in the sandbox image or with the sample’s `files`. When members choose their own names ([Members](./members.html.md#members-that-choose-their-names)), create `/shared` and `/scratch` but not the members’ directories in it: a directory named after a member would tell members the swarm’s names.

[`examples/shared_sandbox.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/shared_sandbox.py) runs [bash()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash) members in one container:

``` python
@task
def shared_sandbox(k: int = 3) -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=[Sample(input=PROMPT, target="9", files={"/shared/notes.md": ""})],
        solver=swarm(
            members=member(react, args={"tools": [bash(timeout=60)]}, count=k),
            controller=leaderless(stop_on_submission=False),
        ),
        scorer=script_works(),
        sandbox=("docker", "compose.yaml"),
        token_limit=1_000_000,
    )
```

Members’ processes run side by side in one container, and nothing stops one member from killing another’s process or filling the disk. Keep the task’s checks and secrets out of a shared sandbox the members could read.

## Per member

With `sandbox`, a member works in a sandbox environment of its own, which becomes its default, so [sandbox()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sandbox) in its tools returns it. `{member}` stands for the member’s name, so `sandbox="{member}"` gives each copy of a counted member its own:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash

from inspect_swarm import member, swarm

solver = swarm(
    members=member(
        react, args={"tools": [bash()]}, name="agent", count=2, sandbox="{member}"
    ),
    channels=[],
)
```

`agent-1` and `agent-2` run in the environments of those names. With `count=1` the member’s name has no number, so `{member}` is `agent`; a task whose member count is a parameter can give each member its own record, `[member(..., name=f"agent-{i}", sandbox=f"agent-{i}") for i in range(1, k + 1)]`, so the names match the environments for every count. The sample’s sandbox configuration provides them (for Docker, a compose service for each), and the swarm checks that they exist when it starts:

``` yaml
services:
  agent-1:
    image: python:3.12-slim
    command: tail -f /dev/null
    network_mode: none
    x-default: true
  agent-2:
    image: python:3.12-slim
    command: tail -f /dev/null
    network_mode: none
```

- When one member has its own sandbox, every member must have one, and no two can have the same one.
- Tools that choose a sandbox without a name, such as [bash()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash), [text_editor()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#text_editor), [bash_session()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash_session) and the agent bridge, use the member’s own.
- The `filesystem` channel describes a shared sandbox, so it is refused: pass `channels=[]`, `channels=[shared_memory()]` for a board the members share, or `filesystem(shared_volume=True)` for [a shared volume](#a-shared-volume).
- The preamble tells each member that it works in its own sandbox, which no other member can reach.

### Shared services

A member cannot see the sample’s other environments, except those in its `visible_sandboxes`, such as a service every member uses. It reaches those only by name, as `sandbox("comparator")`:

``` python
member(
    react,
    args={"tools": [bash()]},
    name="agent",
    count=3,
    sandbox="{member}",
    visible_sandboxes=["comparator"],
)
```

Any member that lists a service can use it, so list only services every member may use. `visible_sandboxes` cannot name another member’s sandbox, or `default`, which inside the member is its own sandbox. [`examples/proof_swarm.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/proof_swarm.py) gives every member a `comparator` that checks answers. The comparator also mounts each member’s workspace volume read-only, so it can check what a member left without any member reaching another’s files.

### A shared volume

When the members’ sandboxes each mount one shared volume, the `filesystem` channel can describe it. Mount the volume at the same path in every member’s service, and pass that path as `shared`:

``` yaml
services:
  agent-1:
    image: python:3.12-slim
    command: tail -f /dev/null
    volumes:
      - shared:/shared
    x-default: true
  agent-2:
    image: python:3.12-slim
    command: tail -f /dev/null
    volumes:
      - shared:/shared
volumes:
  shared:
```

``` python
solver = swarm(
    members=member(react, name="agent", count=2, sandbox="{member}"),
    channels=[filesystem(shared="/shared", shared_volume=True)],
)
```

The preamble then says that `/shared` and the notes file in it are the same in every member’s sandbox. The swarm cannot check that the volume is mounted.

## Sizing

The two topologies cost different resources:

- Shared: one sandbox runs every member’s tool calls at once. Size it for `k` agents working at the same time, not one: CPU, memory, disk, and process limits. A compose service’s `cpus` and `mem_limit` set them for Docker.
- Per member: each sample starts `k` sandboxes, plus any shared services. A sample of 32 members, each with a 32 GiB container, needs 32 such containers at once.

Inspect’s `max_sandboxes` (for Docker, twice the number of CPUs by default) limits how many samples have their sandboxes running at once, not how many containers they hold. With per-member sandboxes, the containers running at once can reach `max_sandboxes × (k + services)`. Lower `max_sandboxes` or `max_samples` to fit the machine or cluster, and keep each member’s container no larger than one agent needs.

## Scoring

The task’s scorer runs after the swarm, outside every member, where [sandbox()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sandbox) is the sample’s `default`. A scorer that grades the members’ work names each member’s sandbox, as in `sandbox("agent-1")`. The result record’s `sandbox` field says which member used which. See [Scoring](./scoring.html.md#per-member-sandboxes).


# Scoring – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

A swarm is scored by the task’s own scorers. The swarm is the task’s solver, so the scorers run after it, on the swarm’s output and on whatever the members left in the sandbox, as they would after a single agent. Inspect Swarm adds no scorer of its own; it records what the swarm did, so analysis can read it beside the scores.

## The answer and the result record

### The answer

The controller’s `final` rule chooses the swarm’s answer from the members’ submissions:

- `first`, the default: the member that submitted earliest, by the swarm’s clock, with ties broken by roster order.
- `last`: the latest submission, again with ties broken by roster order. `leaderless(stop_on_submission=False, final="last")` gives it, for a team whose members build on each other’s work ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#leaderless)).

A controller of your own can also choose the answer itself, with `choose_answer()`, in place of the rule ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#choosing-the-answer)). A member that ended any other way than submitting is never chosen ([Members](./members.html.md#how-a-member-ends)). When no member submitted, the answer is empty. Each answer of a [persistent member](./members.html.md#persistent-members) is a submission for these rules, whatever the member’s status later, and ties between two answers of one member go to the earlier one.

The swarm’s output is the chosen member’s [ModelOutput](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#modeloutput), unchanged, so the scorer sees what it would have seen had that member run alone. The sample’s messages are its input followed by the answer’s message, whose `metadata["inspect_swarm"]` names the mode and the chosen member. Each member’s own conversation is in its timeline.

### The result record

When the swarm ends, it writes a record of what it did to the transcript, as an evidence event in the swarm’s span. Read it with `swarm_result(state)` in a scorer, or `swarm_result(sample)` for a sample read from a log, which needs the sample’s events and attachments. The record is:

``` json
{
  "version": 1,
  "members": [
    {"name": "react-1", "role": null, "choose_name": false, "state": "ended", "status": "submitted", "submitted": true, "time": 41.2, "sandbox": null, "gate_checks": 0, "gate_passes": 0, "first_pass_time": null},
    {"name": "react-2", "role": null, "choose_name": false, "state": "ended", "status": "swarm_cap", "submitted": false, "time": 57.9, "sandbox": null, "gate_checks": 0, "gate_passes": 0, "first_pass_time": null}
  ],
  "final": {"mode": "first", "member": "react-1", "reason": null, "provisional": false}
}
```

- A member’s `state` is `pending` (never started), `running` or `ended`, and `status` says how it ended ([Members](./members.html.md#how-a-member-ends)).
- `time` is seconds from the swarm’s start to the member’s end.
- `choose_name` is `true` for a member that chose its own name ([Members](./members.html.md#members-that-choose-their-names)). `name` is still the swarm’s name for it; the name it chose is in its transcript.
- `sandbox` is the member’s own sandbox, or `null` when it shares the sample’s.
- `gate_checks`, `gate_passes` and `first_pass_time` count the member’s in-loop checks ([Checks during the run](#checks-during-the-run)).
- `final.mode` is `first`, `last` or `controller`, and `final.member` names the chosen member. Under `controller`, `final.reason` is the reason the controller gave. With no submission, `mode` and `member` are `null` and `final.reason` is `"no_submissions"`.

The record is a [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent) with `kind="result_record"`. Its `data` holds the fields above and an `id`, which the swarm also puts in the sample store under `inspect_swarm:result_id`, so that [swarm_result()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_result) finds the record of the store it is given. Older logs hold the record as an [InfoEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#infoevent) with source `inspect_swarm` and `data["type"] == "result_record"`; [swarm_result()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_result) reads both forms. If a limit, error or cancellation ends the swarm before it finalises its answer, the record has the answer so far with `provisional: true`, and that submission is the sample’s output: the first submission so far, the latest under `last`, or the controller’s choice once it has made one.

[swarm_result()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_result) returns `None` when no swarm ran in the sample. It raises `ValueError` for a sample it cannot read the record of: one read without its events or attachments, one written by an inspect_swarm that kept the record in the store under `inspect_swarm:result`, or one that holds a swarm’s events but whose store names no record, as for a sample recovered from a crashed eval.

### The record belongs to the swarm

Only the swarm writes the record and `inspect_swarm:result_id`. Task code (tools, member builders, controllers, scorers) must not write that key, a [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent), or an event with source `inspect_swarm`. Member names, roles and sandboxes, and a controller’s `choose_answer()` reason, must be text that a log keeps as it is: not beginning with `attachment://` or `tc://`, which a log reads as a reference to an attachment, not a base64 `data:` URI, which a log removes when images are not logged, and valid UTF-8. The swarm does not write a record that holds such text, and its end raises `ValueError`.

There is no record while the swarm runs, so no member can read another’s results from it. A scorer that reads it after the swarm is how a task finds each member’s sandbox ([Per-member sandboxes](#per-member-sandboxes)). A tool that reads the transcript sees every member’s model and tool calls anyway. That is a channel between members outside the swarm’s channels, and the swarm records no evidence of it.

## Scoring what members leave

A scorer that reads the sandbox, rather than the answer, scores what every member left there. With the default `leaderless`, the swarm stops the other members at the first submission, so what they were doing is left half done. When the scorer reads a shared artifact, let every member run to its end with `leaderless(stop_on_submission=False)` ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#leaderless)). The swarm returns after every member and its background work have ended, so the scorer sees the sandbox as the members left it.

[`examples/shared_sandbox.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/shared_sandbox.py) scores a script that the members build together in a shared container.

## Per-member sandboxes

With per-member sandboxes, the scorer still runs outside every member, where [sandbox()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sandbox) is the sample’s `default`. A scorer that grades the members’ work names each member’s sandbox. The result record says which member used which, so the scorer can read it rather than repeat the roster:

``` python
@scorer(metrics=[accuracy()])
def tests_pass() -> Scorer:
    """Run the task's tests in each member's sandbox."""

    async def score(state: TaskState, target: Target) -> Score | None:
        # the record exists once the swarm has ended; a member's react(attempts=...)
        # or live control scoring calls this scorer during the solve
        if not state.completed:
            return None
        record = swarm_result(state)
        assert record is not None, "the task's solver is a swarm"
        passed = [
            m.name
            for m in record.members
            if (await sandbox(m.sandbox).exec(["sh", "/tests/run.sh"])).success
        ]
        return Score(value=CORRECT if passed else INCORRECT, metadata={"passed": passed})

    return score
```

A check can also run in a shared service rather than in each member’s sandbox. [`examples/proof_swarm.py`](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/main/examples/proof_swarm.py) mounts each member’s `/workspace` read-only in a `comparator` service, at `/answers/<member>`, and checks an answer there with one command:

``` python
async def run_check(member_sandbox: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Check the answer a member left in its sandbox, with the comparator: whether it is a proof, and why."""
    result = await sandbox("comparator").exec(
        ["python3", "-c", VERIFY, f"/answers/{member_sandbox}/answer.txt"],
        timeout=60,
    )
    return result.success, result.stdout.strip() or result.stderr.strip()
```

`VERIFY` exits 0 only for a proof. Its scorer, `any_member_proved()`, calls `run_check()` for every member in the result record. A member that wrote a valid answer but was stopped before it submitted still passes, which is why the scorer grades every member’s work rather than only the chosen member’s.

## Checks during the run

A task’s scorer can also run inside a member, as `react(attempts=...)` runs it on each submission. For each member, the swarm counts these checks of its own submissions, made in its own loop with the task’s first scorer:

- `gate_checks`: how many submissions were checked.
- `gate_passes`: how many of those passed, a score of 1.0 under Inspect’s default `value_to_float()`.
- `first_pass_time`: the swarm time of the first pass.

They are in the result record and the [metrics](./analysis.html.md#metrics). A member with its own `score_value` can pass its own gate where the count does not, since the count assumes the default converter. Inside a member, a scorer’s [sandbox()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sandbox) is the member’s own.

A scorer that runs during the solve, under `react(attempts=...)`, the other attempt loops or live control scoring, cannot read the result record: [swarm_result()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_result) raises while a swarm in the sample runs. Such a scorer returns `None` until `state.completed` is `True`, as the [per-member sandboxes](#per-member-sandboxes) example does. Inspect drops a `None` score, so the task also needs a scorer that returns a value during the solve, since an attempt loop fails when it gets no score. List that scorer first: the swarm counts checks from the task’s first scorer.

## Comparisons

The swarm’s score is the task’s scorer on the swarm’s answer, or on what the members left for a scorer that reads the sandbox. Compare it with:

- A single agent at the same budget. A swarm of one, `swarm(members=agent, channels=[])`, runs one agent under the swarm’s rules with the same records ([Members](./members.html.md#a-swarm-of-one)), so both arms have a ledger. Unlike a plain agent, it returns an empty output when its member does not submit.
- Epochs of a single agent, through Inspect’s own reducers on the task’s scorer, such as `mean`, `max` and `pass_at_k`:

``` python
from inspect_ai import Epochs, Task, task
from inspect_ai.agent import react
from inspect_ai.scorer import match
from questions import QUESTIONS

from inspect_swarm import swarm


@task
def single_agent() -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=QUESTIONS,
        solver=swarm(members=react(), channels=[]),
        scorer=match(),
        epochs=Epochs(4, ["mean", "pass_at_4"]),
        token_limit=50_000,
    )
```

`pass_at_k` and `max` choose with knowledge of the target, and the swarm’s answer rule does not, so they are upper references, not like-for-like comparisons.

Compare arms on the cost the log records, not on the caps ([Analysis](./analysis.html.md#samples-dataframe)). team@k, the mean member and best@k on graded scores need each member’s own score, which Inspect Swarm does not record yet; best@k can be computed from per-epoch values in [samples_df()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.analysis.html#samples_df).


# Analysis – Inspect Swarm

## Overview

When the swarm ends it writes two entries to the sample store, each also logged as a [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent) of kind `metrics` or `ledger` whose `data` is the entry:

- `inspect_swarm:metrics`: tokens, cost and time for the swarm and each member, and counts of how each member acted, checked its work, communicated and waited ([Metrics](#metrics)).
- `inspect_swarm:ledger`: the swarm’s accounting. Its budget, caps, the usage of each member, model calls that errored or reported no usage, unpriced models, and what stopped the swarm ([The ledger](#the-ledger)).

The result record is an event in the transcript, which `swarm_result(sample)` reads from a sample. It is described in [Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-result-record).

## Metrics

For the swarm:

- `tokens`, `cost`: everything in the swarm: members, controller and final step.
- `wall_clock`: seconds from the swarm’s start to its end.
- `never_acted`: members with no completed model call.
- `steps_to_answer`: completed model calls of the member whose output is the answer, `null` with no answer. For a persistent member’s answer, its calls before that answer.
- `longest_member_steps`: the largest number of completed model calls of any member.
- `critical_steps_to_answer`: the number of completed model calls on the longest chain of calls the answer depended on, across members ([The critical path](#the-critical-path)).

Step counts include cache replays and exclude failed or cancelled attempts. A member’s subagents’ calls count as the member’s. `steps_to_answer` and `longest_member_steps` bound each member’s own sequential depth from above, not the swarm’s: they do not see that one member waited for or read another’s work.

For each member, in roster order:

- `tokens`, `cost`: its usage, its subagents’ and background work’s included.
- `running_time`: seconds from its start to its end, `null` for a member never started.
- `longest_identical_tool_run`: the longest run of identical tool calls (same function and arguments), a sign of a stuck member. `null` for a bridged member: the CLI’s own tool calls are not recorded; bridged host tool calls, such as the swarm’s tools, are.
- `gate_checks`, `gate_passes`, `first_pass_time`: its in-loop checks ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#checks-during-the-run)).
- `comm`, `waits`, `waits_by_outcome`, `wait_time`, `idle_time`: below.
- `holds`, `held_time`: the turn boundaries at which a controller’s callbacks held it, and the seconds it was held. `running_time` includes them ([Boundary callbacks](#boundary-callbacks)). A persistent member’s idle holds count too.
- `activations`, `answers`, `awaiting_work_time`: for a [persistent member](./members.html.md#persistent-members), the activations it began (1 at its start, one more for each wake), the answers it gave, and the part of `held_time` it spent idle, waiting for a wake or its end. All 0 for other members.

### The critical path

`critical_steps_to_answer` is the measure to read latency by: how many model calls the answer took one after another, given that members work in parallel but wait on and build on each other. A member that waits for a peer’s file and then answers in three steps has `steps_to_answer` 3, but if the peer took ten steps to write that file, the answer took at least 11.

Each member’s calls, its subagents’ and background work’s included, form one chain in the order they began. Chains link between members in two ways:

- A channel’s result follows the records it showed, as the channel reports them. It links to each record’s sender at the point the record was committed, so the sender’s work after a send or write is not linked. `shared_memory`: a view of a file follows every write in its history, a view of a deleted file follows the delete, and a `swarm_wait` result follows the write of each file it reports. Directory listings and the `changes` status line make no link. `messages`: `read_messages` follows the messages it returned, and a `swarm_wait` result that reports messages follows every unread message it counts. A message sent with `wake=False` links when it is read, or when a wait that reports messages counts it. A custom channel links what it reports ([Channels](./channels.html.md#writing-a-channel)).
- A `swarm_wait` result that names a member’s end follows all of that member’s calls.

The chain ends when the answering member ends, after its background work has finished, since that work can still change the member’s output. For a persistent member’s answer, it ends at that answer.

The number over-counts work inside a member. Parallel and background subagents, tool calls of one turn, and any other concurrent work count one after another, and the answering member’s background work after its agent returned, its reads included, counts whether or not it changed the answer. That excess reaches peers through the member’s later writes.

The number also misses links. Only channel results and `swarm_wait` make them, so information that members share in other ways adds none: a shared sandbox, a shared volume, a service, a custom channel that reports no dependencies, a shared tool or store key, or a controller that passes one member’s result to another. Counts alone make no link either: the unread-message count and the line of changed files on other results, and `list_members`. Missed links can only lower the number.

With both effects it is not a bound on true causal depth in either direction. A nested swarm’s channels make no link for the outer swarm; its own metrics count it.

It is `null` when there is no answer, when the answering member has no recorded end, when the evidence names a record no recorded commit made (with a warning in the log), and for a sample resumed from a checkpoint. Metrics written by earlier versions do not have it.

### Communication

Each member’s `comm` has an entry, by channel name, for each channel with records, such as `shared_memory`:

- `records` and `record_bytes`: its writes or messages delivered to the channel, and their size.
- `rejections`: its writes or messages the swarm refused, by the control that refused them, such as `rate`.
- `reads` and `listings`: its views of files and of directories, and its `read_messages` results that showed messages.

A member’s subagents count as the member. Every member has an entry for every such channel the swarm opened, zeros included. A swarm with none (`filesystem` only, or `channels=[]`) has `comm` `{}` for every member: communication through files is observed, not recorded, so it is not reported as zero ([Channels](./channels.html.md#shared-files-are-observed-not-recorded)).

### Waits

Each member’s metrics count its `swarm_wait` calls, its subagents’ included:

- `waits`: the number of waits.
- `waits_by_outcome`: that number by what ended each wait: `news` (a changed file or an ended member), `all_waiting`, `stopping`, `member_ending`, `timeout` or `cancelled`. An outcome that ended no wait is left out.
- `wait_time`: the waits’ total seconds. Waits of a member’s subagents that overlap each count.
- `idle_time`: the seconds the member did nothing but wait: its own agent in `swarm_wait`, not yet released, and none of its background work running. A subagent’s wait adds to `wait_time` but not to `idle_time`.

In a swarm with no `swarm_wait` (`filesystem` only, or `channels=[]`) the four are `null`, so 0 means the wait was offered and unused. Waiting is wall-clock time, so a member’s `running_time` includes it.

### Boundary callbacks

When a controller holds a member at turn boundaries ([Controllers](./controllers.html.md#boundary-callbacks)), the swarm writes two kinds of [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent) in the member’s span, with `member` set. Neither holds message text.

`boundary`, once for each boundary where callbacks ran, and for each hold of a persistent member after an answer, callbacks or not:

- `boundary`: the boundary’s index. `after`: what the conversation ended with.
- `origins`: the origins of the callbacks that ran, in order. `held_for`: the seconds the member was held.
- `messages`: the number of messages `before` and `after`.
- `outcome`: `continue` (any change is in the conversation), `end` (with `origin`), `stop`, `error` (a callback raised, or its result was invalid; with `origin` and `error`, the error’s type), `rejected` (applying the change failed, such as at the member’s message limit; with `error`) or `cancelled` (a cancellation from outside the swarm).

`changed`, once for each callback whose result differed from what it received, with its `boundary` and `origin`:

- `added`: each new message’s `id`, `hash` and `index` in the result.
- `removed`: the ids of messages no longer there.
- `replaced`: each message kept under its id with new content, with its `id` and its hashes `before` and `after`.
- `order`: the result’s ids in order, only when the kept messages changed their order.
- `applied`: whether the change is in the member’s conversation. It is `false` when a later callback ended the member or raised, the swarm stopped, or the change was rejected.

A hash is the SHA-256 of the message as the log serializes it, without its id (a value JSON cannot hold counts as null, and text UTF-8 cannot encode is escaped), so a change can be matched to the messages in a later [ModelEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#modelevent)‘s input. When a callback rewrites the conversation, compaction summaries that describe messages it changed are removed, and the removal is one more `changed` event with origin `swarm`. A persistent member’s wake input is a `changed` event with origin `swarm` too, before the callbacks’ own.

### Persistent members

A [persistent member](./members.html.md#persistent-members) writes one `answer` event for each answer, in its span, with `answer`, the answer’s index from 0. In the result record, its [MemberResult](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberresult) has `persistent` true and `answer_times`, the swarm time of each answer. `FinalRecord.answer`, and the `final` event’s `answer`, say which of the chosen member’s answers is the swarm’s; they are `null` for other members.

### Wiring checks

The metrics also check that members are wired to the channels. `tools_unwired` lists, in a swarm with a channel that has tools, the native members with a completed model call whose loops never resolved [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools). Bridged members are exempt, so this metric does not detect a CLI built without [swarm_bridged_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_bridged_tools). A member listed there did not get what the channel offers, so it ran a different experiment from the one configured.

## Samples dataframe

`inspect_swarm.analysis.SwarmColumns` adds each sample’s realized cost and ledger data to Inspect’s [samples_df()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.analysis.html#samples_df). [samples_df()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.analysis.html#samples_df) needs pandas and pyarrow, which Inspect Swarm does not install:

``` bash
pip install "pandas>=2.1.0" "pyarrow>=10.0.1"
```

This example uses a task with a scorer named `match`. Replace `score_match` with your task’s score column (`score_<scorer name>`):

``` python
from inspect_ai.analysis import SampleSummary, samples_df
from inspect_ai.scorer import value_to_float

from inspect_swarm.analysis import SwarmColumns

df = samples_df("logs", columns=SampleSummary + SwarmColumns)
df = df[~df["swarm_resumed"]]
df["score"] = df["score_match"].map(value_to_float(), na_action="ignore")
df.groupby("log")[["score", "swarm_cost"]].mean()
```

The columns:

- `swarm_cost`: the sample’s priced cost in dollars, from its `model_usage`, including scorer calls. Tokens are in [SampleSummary](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.analysis.html#samplesummary)’s `total_tokens`.
- `swarm_complete`: no call is known to be missing from `swarm_cost`. The ledger marks the swarm’s interval complete, and every model in the sample’s `model_usage` is priced. Calls outside the swarm, including scorer calls, are not checked. `False` for a sample with no ledger.
- `swarm_members`: members in the roster.
- `swarm_resumed`: the sample resumed from a checkpoint, so the swarm restarted its caps from zero. Swarms now refuse checkpointing ([Restrictions](./restrictions.html.md)), so only logs from earlier versions can have it true. `False` for a sample with no ledger.
- `swarm_cost_cap`, `swarm_token_cap`, `swarm_time_cap`: the swarm’s caps. The time cap is in seconds.
- `swarm_errored`, `swarm_no_usage`, `swarm_unpriced`: model calls in the swarm that errored or were cancelled (retries included), that completed with no usage, and whose usage has no cost. Each makes the cost a lower bound.
- `swarm_unpriced_models`: models with tokens and no cost, from the ledger and the sample’s `model_usage`, as a JSON list.

The columns read from the ledger are null for a sample with no ledger. A sample that runs two swarms keeps only the last one’s ledger, while its `model_usage` covers both. The columns read the sample’s `store` and `model_usage`, so do not exclude either with `samples_df(exclude_fields=...)`.

The columns hold no per-member data. [swarm_ledger()](./reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#swarm_ledger) reads a sample’s whole ledger as a [SwarmLedger](./reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#swarmledger), whose `members` are [MemberLedger](./reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#memberledger)s with a [Meter](./reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#meter) and [Calls](./reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#calls) each. All are in `inspect_swarm.analysis`, and `SwarmLedger.model_json_schema()` describes every field. For example, each member’s cost:

``` python
from inspect_ai.log import read_eval_log

from inspect_swarm.analysis import swarm_ledger

log = read_eval_log("logs/my-eval.eval")
for sample in log.samples or []:
    ledger = swarm_ledger(sample)
    if ledger is not None:
        for m in ledger.members:
            print(sample.id, sample.epoch, m.name, m.meter.cost)
```

The metrics have no reader of their own; read them from `sample.store["inspect_swarm:metrics"]`.

## The ledger

The ledger of a two-member swarm with a cost cap of \$1 and a time cap of 600 seconds:

``` json
{
  "version": 1,
  "budget": {"cost": 1.0, "tokens": null, "time": 600.0, "reserve": 0.05, "split": "pool", "grace": 120.0, "derive": true},
  "caps": {"cost": 1.0, "tokens": null, "time": 600.0},
  "sample_limits": {"token": null, "cost": null, "message": null, "turn": null, "working": null, "time": null},
  "members": [
    {
      "name": "react-1",
      "status": "submitted",
      "bridged": false,
      "meter": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 1200, "output_tokens": 300, "total_tokens": 1500, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.0081}, "cost": 0.0081, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
      "calls": {"calls": 1, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
      "cancelled": false,
      "background_started": 0,
      "background_cancelled": 0
    },
    {
      "name": "react-2",
      "status": "submitted",
      "bridged": false,
      "meter": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 1150, "output_tokens": 280, "total_tokens": 1430, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.00765}, "cost": 0.00765, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
      "calls": {"calls": 1, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
      "cancelled": false,
      "background_started": 0,
      "background_cancelled": 0
    }
  ],
  "runtime": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": null}, "cost": 0.0, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "final": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": null}, "cost": 0.0, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "swarm": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 2350, "output_tokens": 580, "total_tokens": 2930, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.01575}, "cost": 0.01575, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "calls": {"calls": 2, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
  "unpriced_calls_recorded": 0,
  "sample_delta": {"input_tokens": 2350, "output_tokens": 580, "total_tokens": 2930, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.01575},
  "unattributed": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.0},
  "unpriced_models": [],
  "native_compaction_classes": [],
  "overshoot": {},
  "stop_reason": "submitted",
  "ended_by": null,
  "interrupted": false,
  "final_cancelled": false,
  "resumed": false,
  "total_complete": true,
  "attribution_complete": true
}
```

- `budget` is the [Budget](./reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget) as given. `caps` are the caps the swarm applied, derived from the sample’s limits or given: `cost` in dollars, `tokens`, and `time` in seconds, `null` for no cap. `sample_limits` are the sample’s limits when the swarm started.
- `members` has one entry per member, in roster order. `status` is as in [How a member ends](./members.html.md#how-a-member-ends), `null` for a member never started. `cancelled` means the swarm or the sample cancelled the member, so calls it had in flight are unknown. A hard stop during a background drain also sets `cancelled`; the agent’s returned status is kept. So does a stop or `end()` that cancels a boundary callback while one of its model calls is in flight. `background_started` counts the tasks the member started with [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background), and `background_cancelled` those cancelled before they finished, whose calls in flight are unknown too.
- `meter` is the usage and cost of what a member did. `suspended_cost` is the part spent while token counting was suspended, such as approval calls.
- `calls` counts model calls: `calls` completed ones other than cache replays, `cache_replays` replayed from cache at no charge, `errored` attempts that errored or were cancelled (retries included), `no_usage` completed with no usage, and `unpriced` completed with usage but no cost.
- `runtime` meters the controller’s own calls, `final` the final step’s (the default first-submission answer makes none), and `swarm` everything in the swarm: members, runtime and final step. The top-level `calls` counts every call in the swarm. `unpriced_calls_recorded` counts the unpriced calls the swarm’s meter recorded.
- `sample_delta` is the sample’s usage while the swarm ran. `unattributed` is `sample_delta` minus `swarm`: usage no meter holds, such as the tokens of approval calls.
- `unpriced_models` are models with tokens but no cost. `native_compaction_classes` are loaded model classes that can compact a conversation natively, which logs nothing, so their usage may be missing.
- `overshoot` is how far usage went past each cap, for caps it passed. Calls in flight at a stop can carry usage past a cap.
- `stop_reason` is why the swarm stopped itself: a controller’s `submitted` or `all_done` (as `leaderless` returns), `verified` or `quiescence`, `controller:<reason>` for any other reason a controller returns, `swarm_cap` or `swarm_time`. `ended_by` is what ended it from outside: `sample_limit:<type>`, `operator` for an interrupt, or `unknown`. Each is `null` when it did not happen. Both are set when a sample limit ends the swarm during its own stop.
- `interrupted` means an error (a member’s, the controller’s or the final step’s) or a cancellation ended the swarm before it finished, `final_cancelled` that the final step was cancelled, and `resumed` that the sample resumed from a checkpoint.
- `total_complete` means no call is known to be missing from the totals: nothing was cancelled or interrupted, every call reported priced usage, and no model class can compact natively. Otherwise the totals are lower bounds. `attribution_complete` adds that `unattributed` is zero.


# Restrictions – Inspect Swarm

## What the swarm does not support

- No Inspect background work in bridged members. A member cannot combine Inspect’s [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background) with the agent bridge. [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background) raises in a bridged member, and a member that uses the bridge after starting background work ends `errored`. The CLI’s own background work is a separate gap ([The CLI’s own concurrent work](#the-clis-own-concurrent-work)).
- No checkpointing. Inspect’s sample checkpointing does not restore the swarm’s shared state or its caps, so a swarm raises an error before any member starts in a sample with checkpointing on. Turn checkpointing off for tasks that run a swarm: set `checkpoint=False` on `Task()` or [eval()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.html#eval), or remove every checkpoint setting, including `--checkpoint` and `INSPECT_EVAL_CHECKPOINT`.
- No ACP agents. ACP agents wait for their caller to drive them, so they are refused.
- No scorers that read a member’s tool state. Each member runs in its own tool-state scope, so built-in tools that keep state in the store ([memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory), [bash_session()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash_session), the skill tool) keep each member’s at keys inside its scope, which differ from the default ones. Tool state that a setup solver prepared at the default instance is not carried into the members either; they start with fresh state ([Members](./members.html.md#tool-state)).

## Bridged members

A bridged member runs a CLI agent in the sandbox through Inspect’s agent bridge. `inspect_swe` agents count as bridged by default; pass `member(..., bridged=True)` for other agents that use the bridge. The swarm stops a bridged member by cancelling it.

The CLI’s own tool calls do not emit Inspect [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s, so the tool-event evidence described here does not cover them, Inspect Sentinel does not see them, and `longest_identical_tool_run` is `null` for bridged members.

### Channels for bridged members

A bridged agent’s tools are fixed when it is built, so it does not take [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools). Give it [swarm_bridged_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_bridged_tools) in its bridged tools, naming the channels it uses:

``` python
from inspect_ai.agent import Agent, agent, react
from inspect_ai.tool import bash
from inspect_swe import claude_code

from inspect_swarm import (
    member,
    messages,
    shared_memory,
    swarm,
    swarm_bridged_tools,
    swarm_tools,
)


@agent
def worker() -> Agent:
    return react(tools=[bash(), swarm_tools()])


@agent
def cc_worker(channels: list[str] = ["messages", "shared_memory"]) -> Agent:
    return claude_code(bridged_tools=[swarm_bridged_tools(channels)])


solver = swarm(
    members=[member(worker, count=2), member(cc_worker, name="cc", bridged=True)],
    channels=[messages(), shared_memory()],
)
```

- `"messages"` gives `send_message`, `read_messages` and `list_members`, and `"shared_memory"` gives `shared_memory`. Both give `swarm_wait`. The CLI sees them as the MCP server `swarm`.
- A tool whose channel the swarm does not have returns an error that says so.
- [swarm_bridged_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_bridged_tools) serves only [messages()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#messages) and [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory). [swarm()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm) refuses a bridged member beside a custom channel that has records. Custom channels that only add instructions are fine.
- A bridged member in a swarm with [messages()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#messages) needs `"messages"` too: other members can send to it, and without `read_messages` it could never read them. Its tools return an error that says to add it. `["messages"]` alone, in a swarm that also has the shared memory, is fine, with one cost: the member’s preamble includes every channel’s instructions, so it is still told to use `shared_memory`, which it does not have. Per-member channel instructions are tracked in [\#149](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/issues/149).
- A member uses [swarm_bridged_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_bridged_tools) or [swarm_tools()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#swarm_tools), never both.
- The CLI is one agent to the swarm, whichever of its conversations calls, its subagents included. They share the member’s inbox, so a message any of them reads is read for all. They share what the member has viewed in the shared memory, so a view by a subagent lets the top-level session overwrite or delete that file. Sends and writes from any of them are the member’s.
- A bridged member never counts as waiting, since one call in `swarm_wait` does not show that its CLI is idle. Its waits end on news, a member’s end, the swarm’s stop or their timeout, never because every member is waiting. A native member waiting beside a running bridged member is released by its own timeout at worst.
- The log records these calls as [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s, and their [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent)s have `via` set to `"bridge"` in `data` (in `data.record` for a send). Inspect Sentinel does not see them; the bridge’s `approval=` policies do.

A CLI gives up on an MCP tool call that runs too long, and the model then gets an error in place of the result. Claude Code and Codex both stop one after 300 seconds by default (Claude Code 2.1.308, Codex 0.166.0), while [shared_memory()](./reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#shared_memory) waits up to 600. So a bridged member’s `swarm_wait` lasts at most `swarm_bridged_tools(channels, max_wait=280)` seconds, or the swarm’s longest wait if that is shorter. Native members’ waits are unchanged.

- Claude Code: keep the default. Claude Code stops a call that sends nothing for 300 seconds, and inspect_swe has no setting that raises this for bridged tools; `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` does not.
- Codex: to wait longer, raise its timeout and `max_wait` together: `codex_cli(config_overrides={"mcp_servers.swarm.tool_timeout_sec": "700"}, bridged_tools=[swarm_bridged_tools(channels, max_wait=600)])`.

If the CLI abandons a wait while its host call continues, that call can still mark member ends reported and record dependency links for the CLI’s shared loop. Later conversations may then miss those end notices, and later reads do not repeat those links, even though no model received the abandoned result. The default `max_wait` keeps a wait inside the CLI’s timeout, but it does not confirm delivery, and it does not prevent an abandoned call after an interruption.

Inspect limits shared-memory views to 16 KiB by default. The CLIs also apply token limits (25,000 for Claude Code; 10,000 for Codex), so a view can be shortened further by the CLI. A default `read_messages` result is about 9 KB.

### The CLI’s own concurrent work

The swarm owns and drains only work started with Inspect’s [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background). It does not own, drain or attribute the CLI’s own concurrent work: Claude Code’s background shell commands, background subagents and agent teams, and Codex’s subagents (its multi-agent tools).

- The swarm cannot wait for this work or stop it apart from the CLI. Claude Code waits for much of its background work before it exits, and the member keeps running until then.
- Its model calls go through the member’s bridge, so they count as the member’s usage: against its limits and the swarm’s caps, and in the ledger.
- Work left running can outlast the member. The swarm does not check that the CLI stopped it, and a process started with `nohup` or `&` can keep running after the CLI exits. Such work can change the sandbox after the member ends and before scoring.

To keep a bridged member to work the swarm can see, turn these features off.

Claude Code (checked against 2.1.311, the stable release `claude_code()` installs when the sandbox has none):

- Agent teams are off by default. Claude Code turns them on only with `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` or `--agent-teams`, and `claude_code()` sets neither.
- Background shell commands and background subagents are on by default. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` turns them off, and also stops Claude Code moving long subagents and timed-out commands to the background.
- The `Monitor` tool still runs in the background with that setting. Leave it out with `disallowed_tools=["Monitor"]`.
- Workflows also run subagents, where the account has them. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1` turns them off.

``` python
claude_code(
    env={
        "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS": "1",
        "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS": "1",
    },
    disallowed_tools=["Monitor"],
    bridged_tools=[swarm_bridged_tools(channels)],
)
```

Codex (checked against 0.166.0, the latest release `codex_cli()` installs when the sandbox has none):

- Subagents are on by default. `agents.enabled = false` turns them off: `codex_cli(config_overrides={"agents.enabled": "false"}, bridged_tools=[swarm_bridged_tools(channels)])`. Use this rather than `features.multi_agent = false`, which a model’s catalog entry can override. Only an explicit `features.multi_agent_v2 = true` turns them back on.

None of these settings stop a shell command from starting a process that keeps running on its own, such as `nohup server &`. The swarm does not stop such processes when the member ends.

## What the log records

- Members’ [ToolEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#toolevent)s are the record of what they did, except for bridged members.
- The shared-memory channel’s writes, views and waits are [CommunicationEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#communicationevent)s ([Shared Memory](./shared-memory.html.md#the-record-of-the-board)).
- Files members share in a sandbox, tool instances they share, and a tool that reads the transcript are channels the swarm observes but does not record ([Channels](./channels.html.md#shared-files-are-observed-not-recorded)).

Spans inside a swarm log no [StoreEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#storeevent)s. The swarm’s span logs the net change to the store, which says what changed but not which member changed it. If an error, limit or cancellation escapes the swarm and ends the sample, the log may have no [StoreEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#storeevent) for the swarm’s writes. `sample.store` is always the record of the final store.

## The store keys

The swarm owns three keys in the sample store, written when the swarm ends: `inspect_swarm:result_id`, `inspect_swarm:ledger` and `inspect_swarm:metrics`. Task code must not write them, a [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent), or an event with source `inspect_swarm`. The result record itself is an event in the transcript ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-result-record)). A tool that reads the transcript sees every member’s model and tool calls, a channel between members that the swarm records no evidence of ([Scoring](./scoring.html.md#the-record-belongs-to-the-swarm)).


# inspect_swarm.analysis – Inspect Swarm

## Columns

### SwarmColumns

Columns for `inspect_ai.analysis.samples_df()` with each sample’s realized cost and what the swarm’s ledger says about it, as in `samples_df(logs, columns=SampleSummary + SwarmColumns)`. The `inspect_swarm.analysis` module docstring lists every column.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/analysis/_columns.py#L111)

``` python
SwarmColumns: list[Column] = [
    SampleColumn("swarm_cost", path=_cost, type=float, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_complete", path=_complete, type=bool, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_members", path=_members, type=int, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_resumed", path=_resumed, type=bool, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_cost_cap", path=_cost_cap, type=float, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_token_cap", path=_token_cap, type=float, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_time_cap", path=_time_cap, type=float, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_errored", path=_errored, type=int, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_no_usage", path=_no_usage, type=int, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_unpriced", path=_unpriced, type=int, full=True),
    SampleColumn("swarm_unpriced_models", path=_unpriced_models, full=True),
]
```

## The ledger

### swarm_ledger

Read the swarm’s ledger from a sample.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/analysis/_columns.py#L14)

``` python
def swarm_ledger(sample: EvalSample) -> SwarmLedger | None
```

`sample` [EvalSample](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.log.html#evalsample)  
A sample read from a log with its store, for example from [read_eval_log()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.log.html#read_eval_log). A sample that runs two swarms keeps only the last one’s ledger.

### SwarmLedger

Realized usage and cost of one run of the swarm, and how complete they are.

The swarm writes its ledger once, when it ends, to the sample store as `inspect_swarm:ledger` and as a [SwarmEvent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.event.html#swarmevent) of kind `ledger` whose `data` is the store entry. Read it from a sample with [swarm_ledger()](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#swarm_ledger).

The store entry’s shape follows `version`. This inspect_swarm reads version 1 only.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_ledger.py#L121)

``` python
class SwarmLedger(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`version` Literal\[1\]  
Format version of the ledger.

`budget` [Budget](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget)  
The swarm’s budget as configured.

`caps` dict\[str, float \| None\]  
The swarm’s caps, derived or explicit, keyed by `cost` (dollars), `tokens` and `time` (seconds). `None` for a kind with no cap.

`sample_limits` dict\[str, float \| None\]  
The sample’s limits when the swarm started, keyed by `token`, `cost`, `message`, `turn`, `working` and `time`. `None` for a limit not set.

`members` list\[[MemberLedger](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#memberledger)\]  
Each member, in roster order.

`runtime` [Meter](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#meter)  
Calls made by the swarm’s runtime, such as the controller’s.

`final` [Meter](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#meter)  
Calls made by the final step, which chooses the answer.

`swarm` [Meter](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#meter)  
Every call in the swarm’s context: the members, the runtime, the final step and anything else.

`calls` [Calls](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#calls)  
Model events in the swarm’s span tree: the members, the runtime and the final step.

`unpriced_calls_recorded` int  
Calls the swarm meter recorded with usage but no cost.

`sample_delta` [ModelUsage](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#modelusage)  
The sample’s model usage over the swarm’s lifetime, summed over its models.

`unattributed` [ModelUsage](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#modelusage)  
What the sample used over the swarm’s lifetime that the swarm meter did not record: tokens are `sample_delta` minus `swarm.usage`, and `total_cost` is `sample_delta`’s cost minus `swarm.cost`.

`unpriced_models` list\[str\]  
Models in `sample_delta` with tokens but no cost.

`native_compaction_classes` list\[str\]  
Loaded [ModelAPI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#modelapi) classes that override `compact()`, when the swarm started or ended. Native compaction emits no event, so the ledger cannot count its calls.

`overshoot` dict\[str, float\]  
How far usage at the end went past each cap, keyed by `cost`, `tokens` and `time`. Only kinds over their cap appear.

`stop_reason` str \| None  
The reason the swarm stopped its members, from the first stop begun. `None` when no stop began.

`ended_by` str \| None  
The sample limit (`sample_limit:<type>`) or operator interrupt (`operator`) that ended the swarm, even during its own stop. `unknown` when an outside cause may have ended it but cannot be named. `None` when nothing from outside ended it.

`interrupted` bool  
The swarm did not finish: an error, a limit or a cancellation ended it before or during its final step.

`final_cancelled` bool  
The final step was cancelled.

`resumed` bool  
The sample resumed from a checkpoint, so the swarm restarted its caps from zero. Swarms now refuse checkpointing, so only logs from earlier versions can have it true.

`total_complete` bool  
No call is known to be missing from the swarm’s usage and cost: no member, member background task or final step was cancelled, the swarm was not interrupted, every call completed with priced usage, every model in `sample_delta` is priced, and no loaded model class compacts natively.

`attribution_complete` bool  
`total_complete`, and the swarm meter recorded all the sample used over the swarm’s lifetime: `unattributed` is zero, to within rounding.

### MemberLedger

One member’s entry in the swarm’s ledger.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_ledger.py#L91)

``` python
class MemberLedger(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
The member’s name.

`status` str \| None  
How the member ended (`submitted`, `swarm_cap`, …), or `None` for a member never started.

`bridged` bool  
The member runs a CLI agent through Inspect’s agent bridge.

`meter` [Meter](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#meter)  
Usage and cost of the calls made in the member’s context.

`calls` [Calls](../reference/inspect_swarm.analysis.html.md#calls)  
Model events in the member’s spans.

`cancelled` bool  
The member’s agent was cancelled, or the swarm’s hard stop cancelled its background drain after the agent had returned. A hard stop during the drain keeps the agent’s status, so `cancelled` can be `True` with `status="submitted"`. The agent is cancelled by the hard stop after a grace period, a member time limit or a cancellation from outside the swarm. A bridged member is also cancelled at once when it reaches a cap, its share or one of its own limits, or makes a call after the swarm stopped it.

`background_started` int  
Tasks the member’s agent started with [background()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#background), such as [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent) background subagents.

`background_cancelled` int  
Of `background_started`, the tasks that were cancelled: still running when the member’s drain ended, or cancelled by an error from the member’s work or by the hard stop.

### Meter

Usage and cost recorded by one of the swarm’s meters.

A meter counts the model calls made in its context: one member’s, the runtime’s, the final step’s, or the whole swarm’s.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_ledger.py#L49)

``` python
class Meter(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`usage` [ModelUsage](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.model.html#modelusage)  
Token usage of the calls recorded, except those made while token metering was suspended (approval and review calls).

`cost` float  
Cost in dollars of the priced calls recorded, suspended calls included.

`suspended_cost` float  
The part of `cost` recorded while token metering was suspended (approval and review calls).

### Calls

Counts of the model events in the swarm, or in one member’s spans.

`errored`, `no_usage` and `unpriced` count calls whose cost is missing, so any of them above zero makes the cost a lower bound.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_ledger.py#L67)

``` python
class Calls(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`calls` int  
Model calls that completed, cache replays excluded.

`cache_replays` int  
Model events replayed from the cache (`cache="read"`). They cost nothing.

`errored` int  
Model calls that ended in an error or were cancelled, plus the requests a provider’s client retried inside one call. Their usage is unknown.

`no_usage` int  
Model calls that completed with output but no usage.

`unpriced` int  
Model calls that completed with usage but no cost (`total_cost` is `None`).


# Configuration – Inspect Swarm

## Records

[member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) returns a [Member](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#member), and `swarm(budget=...)` takes a [Budget](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget). They are on their own page because [Member](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#member) and [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) would share a heading anchor on one page.

### Member

A swarm member: a built agent, or a registered `@agent` factory and its arguments.

Create one with [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member), which documents the fields and the member contract.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_member.py#L94)

``` python
class Member(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`agent` [Agent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#agent) \| None  
A built, registered agent. Exactly one of `agent` and `factory` is set.

`factory` AgentFactory \| None  
A registered `@agent` factory, called with `args` to build the member’s agent.

`args` dict\[str, Any\]  
The factory’s keyword arguments.

`name` str \| None  
The member’s name. `None` uses the agent’s or factory’s unqualified registry name.

`role` str \| None  
The member’s role, given to the controller and in the member’s preamble.

`choose_name` bool  
Whether the member chooses its own name. `True` leaves the member’s name out of the swarm’s preamble, which asks it to choose a name and tell the other members; the swarm still uses `name` for everything it records. A controller’s `start(preamble=...)` replaces that preamble with its own text, used as given, or `preamble=False` leaves it out; neither adds a request to choose a name.

`count` int  
How many members this record stands for. Above 1 needs the factory form.

`limits` list\[[Limit](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#limit)\]  
The member’s own limits.

`bridged` bool \| None  
Whether the member’s agent is bridged. `None` counts agents in the `inspect_swe/` namespace as bridged.

`sandbox` str \| None  
The member’s own sandbox environment, where `{member}` stands for the member’s name. `None` shares the sample’s sandbox.

`visible_sandboxes` list\[str\]  
Other sandbox environments the member can reach by name, such as a shared service. Only with `sandbox`.

`persistent` bool  
Whether the member stays available after it answers, held idle until the controller wakes it with `SwarmControl.wake()`.

### Budget

The swarm-wide budget.

By default the swarm derives its caps from the sample’s cost, token and time limits when it starts, holding back `reserve` of each. The caps are stopping rules: when one is reached the swarm stops its members, gives them up to `grace` seconds to finish the calls they have in flight, and then cancels the members still running. If the sample has a time limit, the grace period is capped at half its remaining time.

Every field is a plain value, so each can be a task parameter, and two budgets that differ in any field are logged as different arguments.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_budget.py#L34)

``` python
class Budget(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`cost` float \| None  
Swarm cost cap in dollars. `None` derives it from the sample’s cost limit when `derive` is `True`, and sets no cap when it is `False`.

`tokens` int \| str \| None  
Swarm token cap. A string such as `"output:1m"` is parsed by `parse_token_limit()` and keeps its metering type. `None` derives it from the sample’s token limit, with that limit’s metering type, when `derive` is `True`, and sets no cap when it is `False`.

`time` float \| None  
Seconds after which the swarm stops its members. `None` derives it from the sample’s time limit when `derive` is `True`, and sets no cap when it is `False`.

`reserve` float  
Fraction of each sample limit held back when a cap is derived.

`split` Literal\['pool', 'equal'\] \| tuple\[float, ...\]  
How the cost and token caps are divided between members: one shared pool, equal shares, or one weight per member in roster order. A member that uses up its share stops, and its unused share is not given to the others.

`grace` float  
Seconds members have, at most, to finish calls already in flight after a stop. If the sample has a time limit, this period is capped at half its remaining time.

`derive` bool  
Whether a cap left `None` is derived from the sample’s limit. `False` sets no such cap: the sample’s own limits then end the swarm as they end any solver.


# inspect_swarm – Inspect Swarm

## Swarms and members

### swarm

A swarm of agents working on one sample.

Each member gets a timeline in the sample named after it, so member names must be unique across the swarm runs and other timelines in a sample. To run swarms more than once in one sample, build them with distinct member names. A member may not be named `init`, `solvers` or `scorers`: Inspect’s timelines read spans with those names as the sample’s phases.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swarm/blob/41c5a3e21c8abea5fb39fc4a653538f6ad0a4e2d/src/inspect_swarm/_swarm.py#L48)

``` python
@agent
def swarm(
    members: Member | Agent | Sequence[Member | Agent],
    *,
    controller: str | Controller = "leaderless",
    channels: str | Channel | Sequence[str | Channel] = ("filesystem",),
    budget: Budget = Budget(),  # noqa: B008
) -> Agent
```

`members` [Member](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#member) \| [Agent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#agent) \| Sequence\[[Member](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#member) \| [Agent](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#agent)\]  
The roster: built agents or [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) records. A bare agent is `member(agent)`. A factory-form [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) may stand for several members (`count`).

`controller` str \| [Controller](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#controller)  
How the swarm runs: who starts, when and with what input, and when the swarm is done. A name resolves to a registered controller with its default parameters.

`channels` str \| [Channel](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel) \| Sequence\[str \| [Channel](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#channel)\]  
How members share information. A name resolves to a registered channel with its default parameters. `[]` means none: members get no channel instructions, though a shared sandbox is still shared.

`budget` [Budget](../reference/inspect_swarm.configuration.html.md#budget)  
The swarm-wide cap.

### member

A swarm member, with a name, role, limits or count.

A member is a built agent, `member(react(prompt=...))`, or a registered `@agent` factory and its arguments, `member(deepagent, args={"tools": [bash()]}, count=4)`. Both must be registered with `@agent`, so that the log can name them and replay can find them. A built agent can also be passed to `swarm(members=...)` without [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member).

No agent object runs twice at the same time in one sample. A built agent is one member: it is built once, when the task is built, and shared by concurrent samples, as any Inspect solver is. The same agent object cannot be in two members. Several copies of one configuration (`count` above 1) need the factory form: the swarm calls `factory(**args)` once for each member in each sample, so each copy gets its own agent and whatever the factory builds. [member()](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#member) checks the arguments against the factory’s signature but does not call it, so the factory’s own checks run when the member is built.

Names. Members left on their default name are numbered across the whole roster, not per record, so one member with different arguments takes two records: `[member(react, args={"prompt": a}, count=6), member(react, args={"prompt": b, "model": m})]` is `react-1` to `react-7`. When every copy differs, give each its own record, as in `[member(react, args={"prompt": p}) for p in prompts]`. Names given with `name` are not numbered across records, so give each record its own.

Objects given to an agent are shared. Every member built from one record receives the same objects from `args`, and two built agents given the same tool object share it, across members and samples. Inspect’s built-in tools keep their state in the sample store or the sandbox, so this matters only for a custom tool or helper that keeps state in its Python object (a counter, a cache, a client). To give each member its own, construct it inside a member builder, an `@agent` factory that builds the configured agent, and use the factory form.

Tool state. Each member runs in its own tool-state scope, named after the member. Built-in tools that keep state in the sample store ([memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory), [bash_session()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash_session), the skill tool) give each member its own state when their `instance` is left at the default, so the default [memory()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#memory) is private to each member. An explicit `instance` is used as given: members, or the copies of one counted member, that name the same instance share its state, so a board shared on purpose is `memory(instance="board")`. The sample store itself is shared. State that custom tools or agent code keep in the store with no instance is shared unless they resolve their instance with [tool_state_instance()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#tool_state_instance). Built-in tool state that a setup solver prepared at the default instance before the swarm runs is not visible to the members.

Submissions. A member that returns normally has submitted, and its output is its answer, unless the output’s stop reason is `content_filter` or `model_length`. That is how [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react) returns after three refusals or a context overflow it could not recover from, so the member ends `unsubmitted` and the swarm never chooses its output as the answer. Other agents keep the rule that a normal return is a submission: an agent that gives up in some other way and returns is treated as having answered. A persistent member’s normal return is never a submission: its answers are recorded as it gives them, so a loop that returns has stopped without one (an `on_continue` that returns `False`, for example), and the member ends `unsubmitted`, its earlier answers still candidates.

Persistent members. With `persistent=True`, the member stays available after it answers: when it submits in a turn that calls no handoff, or a `react(submit=False)` member gives a tool-free reply, the swarm records that as one of its answers and holds the member idle at its next turn boundary, in the same agent loop. The controller hears [MemberIdle](../reference/inspect_swarm.html.md#memberidle) and gives the member its next piece of work with `SwarmControl.wake()`, which appends it to the member’s conversation. Every answer is a candidate for the swarm’s answer. The member’s limits span its whole life, and its time limit does not run while it is idle. A member stopped or ended while idle ends `submitted`, its last answer as its output. Only a member whose agent is a [react()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#react), `react(submit=False)` or [deepagent()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.agent.html#deepagent) loop without background dispatch, given directly or returned by an `@agent` builder, can be persistent; any other agent, and a bridged member, is refused.

Stopping itself. An agent that raises `LimitExceededError("custom", ...)` with no `source` to stop itself ends only its member, with status `member_limit:custom`; the other members continue and the swarm never chooses its output as the answer. This holds when the error is raised in a task group inside the agent, too.

Sandboxes. Members share the sample’s sandbox by default. With `sandbox`, a member works in its own: the swarm makes that environment the member’s default, so [sandbox()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.util.html#sandbox) in its tools returns it, and hides the sample’s other environments from the member except those in `visible_sandboxes`, such as a shared service. Tools that choose a sandbox without a name, such as [text_editor()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#text_editor), [bash_session()](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/reference/inspect_ai.tool.html#bash_session) and the agent bridge, use the member’s own; a visible service is reached only by name. `sandbox="{member}"` gives each copy of a counted member the environment named after it: `member(factory, name="agent", count=2, sandbox="{member}")` runs `agent-1` and `agent-2` in the environments of those names. The sample’s sandbox configuration provides the environments (for Docker, a compose service for each), and the swarm checks that they exist when it starts. When one member has its own sandbox, every member must have one, no two the same, and the `filesystem` channel, which describes a shared sandbox, can be used only as `filesystem(shared_volume=True)`, for sandboxes that each mount one shared volume. A service in `visible_sandboxes` is reachable from any of the member’s tools that take a sandbox name, so list only services every member may use.

Chosen names. With `choose_name=True` the member is not told its name: the swarm’s preamble says how many agents are in the swarm and asks it to choose a name for itself and tell the other members, and the `filesystem` channel tells it to keep its work in a directory named with the name it chose.
